## Quadratic construction explaining the seven-point example

In complex notation, take p,q with rational lengths of
p, q, p+q, p-q, 2p+q, p+2q.
The old six-point construction supplies lengths 87,85,68,158,131,127,
respectively, e.g. p=87, q=(-1695+40 sqrt(-2002))/29.
The following seven complex points have all rational mutual distances, because
every difference factors into the listed linear forms:

```
0, pq, -p(p+q), -q(p+q), -2p², -2q², -2(p+q)².
```

At the specified p,q they are in general position and are similar to the
certified seven-point set. This symbolic construction has not itself been
formalized, but the explicit resulting configuration is formally certified.

## Restricted S-unit search

`sunit_search.py` studies rational functions in t=p/q, whose zeros and poles
are contained in {infinity,0,-1,1,-1/2,-2}. Norms of these factors at t are rational.
It enumerates coprime S-smooth numerators and denominators of degree <=4 for
which F and 1-F are S-units, obtaining 264 nonconstant functions.
There are 2400 pairwise edges after rejecting collinearities and concyclicity
with anchor points 0 and 1. It finds seven-point sets, but no eight-point set
within this family. This is a computational observation, not a Lean theorem.
The degree bound is suggested by polynomial abc/Mason-Stothers; no completeness
claim has been formalized. This does NOT bound arbitrary integral-distance sets.

## Other newly formalized obstructions

`rational_one_add_fourth_not_square` proves 1+t^4 is not a rational square for
nonzero rational t, using Mathlib's `not_fermat_42` after clearing denominators.
`hyperbola_antipodal_distance_irrational` consequently forbids antipodal doubling
on the fixed rectangular hyperbola xy=1. In particular, do NOT assume that
adding -t parameters preserves rational distances: the pair t,-t needs the
impossible fourth-power square condition.

`erdos213For_of_pythagorean_products` is a verified sufficient condition using
injective rational parameters t_i>1 with 1+(t_i t_j)^2 rational squares for all
distinct i,j. No arbitrary-size such parameter sets have been constructed.

The original reciprocal-product extension t4=1/(t1*t2*t3) preserves those square
conditions but forces the four hyperbola points to be concyclic.

## Parallel-line extension experiment

`parallel_extension.py` generates intersections of lines through pairs of
existing vertices, parallel to rational-length directions. At level 1, the
allowed directions are the existing edges. At level 2, products and conjugate
products of these complex directions are also allowed; multiplicativity of
the norm preserves rational lengths. All checks use exact fractions.

- Six-point set, level 1: 6 directions, 79 new candidate points; only the center
  has rational distances to all six, and it violates general position.
- Six-point set, level 2: 46 directions, 26,699 candidates; again only the center.
- Seven-point set, level 1: 18 directions, 3,972 candidates; no rational extension.
- Seven-point set, level 2: 269 directions, 1,468,824 candidates; no rational extension.

These are restricted finite searches, not nonexistence proofs for arbitrary
rational extensions or for larger unrelated configurations. Spec.lean was not
changed by these experiments and its main theorem remains unresolved.

## Near-extension analysis of the original symbolic family

`near_extension.py` enumerates the anchored seven-point configurations in the
original 264-function S-unit family. Geometry is tested exactly at the fixed
quadratic parameter used in the certificate. It finds 168 seven-point sets.
For every candidate additional point that satisfies general position with such
a set, at least three of its distances to that set fail the symbolic smooth-
factor test. The histogram of missing edges, over (set,candidate) pairs, is:

- three missing edges: 2880;
- four missing edges: 5664;
- five missing edges: 30336.

Thus this family does not supply a seven-to-eight extension with only one
unresolved symbolic distance. This is a restricted observation: it does not
classify candidates outside the family, nor every geometric specialization.

`near_norm_classes.py` further analyzes the 2880 closest candidates. Put
R=|t|^2 and S=|t+1|^2. Norms of polynomial factors in t are computed as
resultants against t^2-(S-R-1)t+R. The five already-square norm factors are
R, S, 2R+2-S, 2R+2S-1, and 2S-R+2. After removing these and even-multiplicity
factors, the three missing norms have independent parity vectors of irreducible
polynomial factors in every case. There are 5184 distinct tested missing edges
and 78 new irreducible factors. This shows there is no generic simplification
to one new square condition by multiplication of the old ones in these cases;
it does NOT exclude special parameter values satisfying all three conditions.
No part of this computation has been asserted as a Lean theorem.

## Symbolic geometry of the seven-point formula

`seven_determinants.py` factors all 35 triangle and 35 circle determinants for

    0, t, -t(t+1), -(t+1), -2t^2, -2, -2(t+1)^2.

After removing the common nonreal-parameter factor, all irreducible factors
are among the following sixteen polynomials in R=|t|^2, S=|t+1|^2:

    R, S, R+S+1,
    2R+2S-1, 2R-S+2, R-2S-2,
    R-1, S-1, R-S,
    R+S-1, R-S+1, R-S-1,
    2R-S-1, R+S-2, R-2S+1,
    F = R^3-R^2*S-R^2-R*S^2-R+S^3-S^2-S+1.

Only the quadruple (0,-2t^2,-2,-2(t+1)^2) contributes the last cubic factor.
The other factors record norm positivity, equal-side conditions, right-angle
conditions, or analogous linear relations. These identities clarify the
geometric exclusions for the known formula but do not increase its cardinality.
Sage identifies the Jacobian of the homogenized cubic F=0 with the conductor-36
curve y^2=x^3-15x+22, of rank zero and torsion order six. This has not been
formalized and is not used as an assumption or theorem in Spec.lean.

A possible elliptic fibration of the rational-median-triangle parameter surface
was also identified algebraically. With side lengths r,s,q and auxiliary length
u satisfying u^2+s^2=2r^2+2q^2, impose

    s=(17r-7q)/13, u=(7r+17q)/13.

The two remaining squared-length conditions become

    (13v)^2 = 916r^2-476rq-71q^2,
    (13w)^2 = 409r^2-476rq+436q^2.

The known point (r,q,s,u,v,w)=(87,85,68,158,131,127) lies on this
intersection of two quadrics. No new general-position configuration or
arbitrary-cardinality construction has been obtained from this fibration.

The main conjecture remains unresolved. Spec.lean is unchanged and still has
its original `sorry`; no proof submission was made in this continuation.

## Conditional eight-point template from oblique-grid directions

The symbolic S-unit test with finite roots

    {0, -1, 1, -1/2, -2, 1/2, 2}

has 888 nonconstant functions and 16080 admissible symbolic edges (geometry
checked at the usual nonreal parameter). It finds this eight-point template:

    0,
    1,
    -4/((t-2)(t+2)),
    -4/(t-2),
    -2/((t-2)(t+1)),
    2(t-1)/(t-2),
    -2(2t-1)/((t-2)(t-1)),
    -4(t-1)/(t-2)^2.

Every difference factors using only t, t±1, t±2, and 2t±1. Hence rational
norms of these seven factors suffice for all 28 distances to be rational.
Together with the constant direction 1, these are precisely the eight direction
lengths needed for a 3-by-3 oblique grid generated by t and 1 to be a rational-
distance set. Such a grid itself has collinear triples; the template is a
separate transformation intended to avoid those degeneracies.

**This is conditional, NOT an eight-point integral-distance example.** At the
usual seven-point parameter, the two new squared norms are

    |t-2|^2   = 56809/7225,
    |2t-1|^2 = 57841/7225,

which are not rational squares. No suitable new nonreal parameter has been
constructed. General position is verified computationally for the displayed
formulas at the usual parameter, but that parameter fails the new distance
conditions; this cannot be combined into an existence claim.

## Rational unit-direction intersection tests

A new search constructs candidates as intersections of a line through 0 in
rational unit direction u and a line through 1 in rational unit direction v.
For u=(ux,uy), v=(vx,vy), the point is

    u * vy/(ux*vy-uy*vx).

The denominator is required to be nonzero. Its distances to 0 and 1 are
rational automatically. Pairwise distances are then checked exactly by
integer square roots, and general position by homogeneous integer determinants.
These scripts use individual coordinate denominators rather than a potentially
huge common denominator.

## Square factors beyond the S-unit family

The earlier S-unit searches impose a genuine restriction: a squared factor has
rational norm at a quadratic-imaginary specialization even when the original
factor does not. Thus S-unit degree bounds do not classify all rational-norm
rational functions.

`Submission/SquareFactors.lean` proves the following broader parametrization.
If Re(u)=r and normSq(u)=s are rational, and 1+u² != 0, set

    F(u) = (2u/(1+u²))²,
    delta = (s-1)²+4r².

Then the exact distances are

    dist(F(u),0) = 4s/delta,
    dist(F(u),1) = ((s+1)²-4r²)/delta.

The identity 1-F(u)=((1-u²)/(1+u²))² explains both rationalities.
`candidate_rational_distances` also handles the zero-denominator case according
to Lean's total division convention. `candidate_distances` and
`candidate_rational_distances` compile with only the three permitted axioms.
The log is `/tmp/square_factors_lean.log`. This standalone development file is
not imported by Spec.lean.

`square_factor_extension.py` tests this construction exactly in Q(sqrt(-2002)).
The source parameters are u=z+b, for z among the previous 264 S-unit values and
b in {0,1,-1}. It also includes conjugation and the six transformations
permuting anchors {0,1,infinity}. After duplicates and previous points are
removed, this yields 3672 additional candidates. Exact rational-square tests
independently verify their distances to both anchors.

The full anchored graph has 3936 vertices and 2544 admissible edges. Of these,
2502 are the previous edges, 42 join an old and a new candidate, and none join
two new candidates. Thus this tested enlargement gives no eight-point set.
Here 'admissible' also excludes collinearity with either anchor and concyclicity
with both anchors. The full test does not merely filter to candidates with
many old neighbors. Data: `/tmp/square_factor_extension_1.json`; log:
`/tmp/square_factor_full.log`.

This is another restricted exact experiment, NOT a nonexistence theorem.
No arbitrary-cardinality construction or scale-independent upper bound has
been obtained. Spec.lean remains unchanged, including its original main
`sorry`; no completed proof has been submitted.

## General characteristic-coordinate normalization (Lean-verified development)

`Submission/Normalization.lean` develops a general reduction, rather than a
finite candidate search. It uses only `import FormalConjecturesUtil` and is
not imported by Spec.lean.

The theorem `integral_complex_normalization` proves: for any integral-distance
set S in the complex plane containing a noncollinear triangle, there exist
positive natural numbers D,L and a real affine equivalence f such that

    dist(f(z),f(w)) = L*dist(z,w),
    f(z) = x + y*sqrt(D)*I  for integers x,y, whenever z belongs to S.

No finiteness assumption is needed for this theorem. The normalizing scale is
a positive integer, not a normalization of a shortest distance to one.
`integral_plane_normalization` transports it to the conjecture's Euclidean
plane. `general_position_integer_coordinates` preserves finiteness, cardinality,
integer distances, and both general-position conditions.

The arithmetic behind the normalization is explicit. For anchors a,b,c, write
K=dist(a,b), M=dist(a,c), N=dist(b,c), and

    C = K²+M²-N²,
    D = 4K²M²-C² > 0.

With frame(z)=conj(b-a)*(z-a), let alpha=2*Im(frame(c)), so alpha²=D.
For a point p, put R=dist(a,p), U=dist(b,p), V=dist(c,p) and

    A = K²+R²-U²,
    B = M²+R²-V²,
    X = D*A,
    Y = 2K²*B-C*A.

The similarity z -> 2D*frame(z), of integer scale 2DK, has coordinates
(X,Y*alpha). Since alpha=±sqrt(D), these are integer characteristic coordinates.
The proof uses polynomial identities for real and imaginary parts of frame.

The file also proves `exists_injective_integer_projection`: for finite jointly
injective integer coordinate pairs (x_i,y_i), some integer m makes

    (m²-D)*x_i - 2mD*y_i

injective in i. Its proof excludes finitely many roots of the nonzero quadratic
polynomials arising from pairs i != j. `integer_lattice_similarity` implements
this as complex multiplication by

    (m²-D) + 2m*sqrt(D)*I,

whose norm is the positive integer m²+D. The transformed second coordinate is

    2m*x_i + (m²-D)*y_i.

The final theorems `integer_coordinates_with_injective_projection` and
`general_position_integer_coordinates_injective` combine these facts: requiring
integer characteristic coordinates AND distinct first coordinates does not
restrict the existence problem for finite general-position integral-distance
sets with at least three points.

The check log is `/tmp/normalization.log`; axiom checks are included in the file.
The exact determinant-certificate converse has not been packaged here, and no
bound on D, coordinate height, diameter, or cardinality is obtained. Thus this
normalization theorem does NOT settle Erdős 213. Spec.lean remains unchanged
with its original main `sorry`; no completed proof has been submitted.

## Exact arithmetic certificate equivalence (Lean-verified)

`Submission/ArithmeticReduction.lean` now proves

    Erdos213.erdos213For_iff_arithmetic {n : Nat} (hn : 3 <= n) :
      Erdos213For n <-> ArithmeticConfiguration n.

`ArithmeticConfiguration n` consists solely of the following integer data:

- D : Nat with D > 0;
- x,y : Fin n -> Int, with x injective;
- d : Fin n -> Fin n -> Nat;
- all triangle determinants nonzero for distinct triples;
- all circle determinants nonzero for distinct quadruples;
- (x_i-x_j)^2+D*(y_i-y_j)^2=d_ij^2 for every pair.

These are exactly the conditions used by the existing sufficient certificate.
The new necessity proof uses the general normalization and injective projection
proved in Normalization.lean, enumerates the resulting finite set, and extracts
integer distances. The geometric determinant converses are now checked too:
noncollinearity gives a nonzero triangle determinant; if the first three points
are noncollinear, a zero circle determinant yields a circle through all four.

For the latter converse, with Delta the triangle determinant, the center is

    a + ((|a-b|^2*(c_y-a_y)-|a-c|^2*(b_y-a_y))/(2*Delta),
         (|a-c|^2*(b_x-a_x)-|a-b|^2*(c_x-a_x))/(2*Delta)).

The proof first expands the difference of squared distances to this center,
then uses its two linear defining equations. This avoids unnecessarily expanding
squared rational expressions. All axiom checks succeed with only
`propext`, `Classical.choice`, and `Quot.sound`.

The file has 841 lines and one import, `FormalConjecturesUtil`. It is standalone:
it contains a copy of the unchanged Erdos213For definition and the certificate
helpers from Spec.lean, followed by the normalization proofs and the arithmetic
converse. It does NOT contain the unresolved main theorem or a new existence
claim. The compile log is `/tmp/arithmetic_reduction.log`. No `sorry` or extra
axiom occurs in this development file.

This completes the coordinate-certificate reduction, but not the conjecture.
There is still no bound on D, coordinate heights, or certificate cardinality,
and no construction for arbitrarily large n. No new finite candidate search was
performed in this continuation. Spec.lean and its original main `sorry` remain
unchanged; no completed proof has been submitted.

## Quadratic S-unit templates and exact norm criterion (new continuation)

The three pending degree-six searches completed. Their finite linear roots were
`{0,-1,1,-1/2,-2}` and the additional irreducible quadratic was as follows:

- `t^2+t+1`: 540 nonreal functions, 9360 admissible edges; an eight-point
  conditional template was found.
- `t^2+1`: 360 functions, 3180 edges; no eight-point result in the tested family.
- `t^2-t-1`: 366 functions, 3540 edges; no eight-point result in the tested family.

The first template, after multiplication by `-(t^2-1)`, is

```
0, 1-t^2, (t+2)^2/3, t+2, (t+2)(t+1), t+1, 2t+1, t^2+t+1.
```

All 28 differences factor into rational constants and

```
t, t+1, t-1, t+2, 2t+1, t^2+t+1.
```

Conversely, each of these six factors occurs itself as a point difference.
Consequently rationality of their six norms is NECESSARY AND SUFFICIENT for
rationality of all the template's mutual distances.

The extra factor occurs on four disjoint edges: `(0,7), (1,3), (2,5), (4,6)`.
The `(2,5)` edge has the extra factor divided by 3. Thus the template is NOT
an extension of the existing seven-point witness by a single extra point.

`Submission/QuadraticTemplate.lean` (611 lines, standalone, one import) now
formally proves this equivalence as `all_pairwise_norms_iff` and
`rational_distances_iff`. It also proves:

- `point_injective`: a nonreal parameter with rational norm of `t-1` gives
  eight distinct points. The proof excludes `t^2+t+1=0` using the irrationality
  of sqrt(3), then uses all 28 factorizations.
- `extra_norm_iff_discriminant`: if `|t|=a` and `|t+1|=c` with rational a,c,
  the extra norm is rational iff
  `a^4+c^4+1-a^2*c^2-a^2-c^2` is a square in Q.
- `oldParameter_norms`: all five old norm conditions hold at
  `t=(-29493-696*sqrt(-2002))/41905`, with respective norms
  `87/85,68/85,158/85,127/85,131/85`.
- `oldParameter_extra_normSq`: at that same parameter,
  `|t^2+t+1|^2=7778281/52200625`, whose numerator factors as `7*1111183`.
- `oldParameter_extra_not_rational` and
  `oldParameter_not_eight_rational_points`: the old parameter DOES NOT supply
  a rational-distance eight-point witness. This failure is Lean-verified,
  not just a numerical observation.
- `symmetric_not_nontrilinear`: under the nonreal/rational-`t-1` assumptions,
  the three isosceles specializations `Re(t)=-1/2`, `|t|^2=1`, and
  `|t+1|^2=1` each force a distinct collinear triple. The triples are,
  respectively, indices `(1,3,5)`, `(4,5,6)`, and `(0,5,7)`.

All axiom checks in `/tmp/quadratic_template_lean.log` succeed using only
`propext`, `Classical.choice`, and `Quot.sound`. The file has no holes.
The generator `/tmp/make_quadratic_lean.py` produces only the core norm results;
`/tmp/append_quadratic_lean.py` adds the geometric obstructions, but subsequent

### Rational-median families from a genus-one fibration

Write a,b,c for side lengths and u,v,w for twice the median lengths. Start from

```
u^2=2a^2+2b^2-c^2,
v^2=2a^2-b^2+2c^2,
w^2=-a^2+2b^2+2c^2.
```

The hyperplane `v=(2+k)a-(1+k)b-kc` factors the middle equation as

```
(a-b-c)*((k^2+4k+2)a-(k^2+2k+2)b-(k^2-2)c)=0.
```

On the nondegenerate component, c is a rational linear combination of a,b.
Setting b=1 leaves two quadratic square conditions, hence a genus-one curve.
Parametrizing the first conic through a degenerate rational point gives a
quartic for the remaining median. Interpolating a quadratic through three
rational boundary sections gives another rational point of this quartic.

The exact Sage script `median_low_degree.sage` found 21 distinct function pairs
(a,c) from these interpolations, with minimum degree five (12 families).
An earlier triple-tangent construction, `median_euler_family.sage`, gave a
higher-degree family; it was not useful for the extra norm condition.

Data and logs:

```
/tmp/median_euler_family.log
/tmp/median_euler_family.sobj
/tmp/median_low_degree.log
/tmp/median_low_degree.sobj
```

These twelve families are NOT a parametrization of all rational-median
triangles. They are only explicit rational curves on the median surface.

### A simpler representative and Lean-verified identities

After r=k+1 and clearing a common denominator, one degree-five family is

```
A = r^5+r^4-6r^3+26r^2+9r+9
B = 2(3r^4+10r^2-9)
C = r^5-r^4-6r^3-26r^2+9r-9
U = r^5+3r^4+26r^3-18r^2+9r+27
V = -2r(r^4-10r^2-27)
W = r^5-3r^4+26r^3+18r^2+9r-27.
```

The three median identities hold identically. Its extra discriminant is

```
A^4+B^4+C^4-A^2*B^2-A^2*C^2-B^2*C^2 = (r^2-3)^2*F(r),

F(r)=r^16-76r^14+1956r^12+27308r^10+67030r^8
     +245772r^6+158436r^4-55404r^2+6561.
```

The Heron polynomial factors as

```
128r^2(r^2-9)(r^2-1)(r^2+1)(r^2+9)
    *(r^4-22r^2+9)*(r^4+2r^2+9),
```

which is strictly positive for rational 1<r<3; B is also positive there.
The reciprocal symmetry yields, for r != 0,

```
F(r)=r^8*P(r^2+9/r^2),
P(s)=s^4-76s^3+1920s^2+29360s+31984.
```

`Submission/MedianFamily.lean` formally proves all these identities, area
positivity, and the EXACT equivalences between the discriminant square
condition, `IsSquare (F r)`, and (for r != 0) `IsSquare (P(r^2+9/r^2))`.
It also proves that r=0,+/-1,+/-3 are degenerate, WITHOUT claiming these are
all rational points. It is standalone with one FormalConjecturesUtil import,
no holes, and only the permitted axioms. Log: `/tmp/median_family_lean.log`.

This auxiliary file does not prove general position of the eight-point
construction, does not assert existence of a nondegenerate square value,
and does not contain the unresolved main theorem.

## Independent bounded median enumeration and quadratic-factor catalog

This continuation did NOT settle the conjecture and did not change Spec.lean.
No new unconditional existence theorem was obtained.

### Primitive rational-median triangles up to side 20000

`search_median_triangles.cpp` enumerates primitive scalene integer-side triangles
whose three medians are rational. If a side is a and its doubled median is u,
then `3a^2+u^2=K=2(a^2+b^2+c^2)`. The search groups integer pairs (a,u) by K,
then finds triples of side squares summing to K/2. For primitive triangles an
odd side exists; its doubled median is odd, so K=4 mod 8. This gives the parity
filter used by the code. Degenerate and nonprimitive triples are discarded.

At largest-side bound 20000 it generated 286980267 packed records (about 2.3 GB),
sorted and searched them in about 24 seconds, and returned 121 primitive
scalene triangles. None had a square value of

```
a^4+b^4+c^4-a^2*b^2-a^2*c^2-b^2*c^2.
```

All 121 output rows were independently checked in Python for positivity,
strict triangle inequalities, primitivity, the three median equations, and the
nonsquare discriminant. The computation is NOT a Lean-certified exhaustive
classification, and no conclusion beyond the stated bound is asserted.

Files:

```
search_median_triangles.cpp
/tmp/median_triangles_20000.txt
/tmp/median_triangles_20000.log
```

### Catalog of additional quadratic factors

`quadratic_factor_catalog.sage` generates S-smooth polynomials A,B of degree at
most six over the original five finite linear factors. For constants selected
by an unused old root or leading-coefficient cancellation, it factors A-cB,
removes old linear factors, and retains quadratic residual factors (or powers
of a quadratic). This gives 664 primitive integer quadratics, including
reducible and repeated-root quadratics. The improved version
`quadratic_factor_catalog_v2.sage` also explicitly handles powers of reducible
quadratics; it gives the SAME 664 polynomials.

This construction is a finite catalog, NOT a proof that every possible
additional quadratic arises this way. In particular, constants for pencils
with no old root or infinity cancellation are not exhaustively treated.

For `Q(t)=A*t^2+B*t+C` and a triangle with `|t|=a/b`, `|t+1|=c/b`, put
`T=c^2-a^2-b^2`. The exact integer numerator of `|Q(t)|^2*b^4` is

```
A^2*a^4+B^2*a^2*b^2+C^2*b^4+A*B*a^2*T+B*C*b^2*T
  +A*C*(T^2-2*a^2*b^2).
```

The catalog was tested for a square numerator at all six orderings of each of
the 121 triangles. Exactly 54 catalog quadratics had hits. Twelve are squares
of linear polynomials and therefore work for every triangle. The other 42
only work at the four shapes

```
(68,85,87), (127,131,158), (113,243,290), (244,367,523).
```

The first two form a median-dual pair, as do the last two. In addition to the
two factors already studied, the old parameter has rational norm of
`11*t^2+7*t+2`, with numerator square root 52286 in the above normalization.
At the triangle (113,243,290), `t^2+1` has rational norm.

## Verified parabola reduction

`Submission/Parabola.lean` is a new, standalone, hole-free 323-line development.
It duplicates the definition and rational-to-integer scaling infrastructure,
so should not be imported together with the other standalone developments.
It proves, for `point t = (t,t²)`:

- `dist_sq`: squared distance is `(s−t)²(1+(s+t)²)`;
- `not_collinear`: three distinct parameters give noncollinear points;
- `cospherical_iff`: four distinct parameters give concyclic points iff their
  sum is zero (both directions, with an explicit center for the converse);
- `rational_distance_iff`: for distinct rational s,t, distance is rational iff
  `1+(s+t)²` is a rational square;
- `erdos213For_of_sums`: an injective n-tuple of rational parameters satisfying
  those pairwise square conditions and no zero four-term sum yields
  `Erdos213For n`;
- `erdos213For_of_positive_sums`: positive parameters automatically satisfy
  the four-term condition;
- `erdos213For_of_quadratic_squares`: positive rationals u,v and rational square
  values of `(k+u)²+v²` for every integer `1 ≤ k ≤ 2*n−3` suffice. The parameters
  are `t_i = (i+u/2)/v`.

The last condition is only sufficient. Its existence for arbitrary n has NOT
been proved. In particular this reduction does not supply an eight-point set
or settle the main conjecture. The printed dependencies of the main new lemmas
are exactly `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`.

Log: `/tmp/parabola_lean.log`.

`Spec.lean` remains unchanged in this continuation, with its original main
`sorry`. No completed proof or disproof has been submitted.

## Genus-three Jacobian route (new continuation; still NOT SOLVED)

### Exact algebraic link

Put `z=2*t+1` and write its monic quadratic as `U(X)=X²+bX+c`.
For a nonreal conjugate pair (`b²<4c`), the extra-quadratic eight-point template
requires exactly these rational squares:

```
c, 1+b+c, 1−b+c, 9+3b+c, 9−3b+c, (c−3)²+3b².
```

The first five are `U(0), U(1), U(−1), U(3), U(−3)`. The last is the norm of
`U` at the roots of `X²+3`. This leads to the genus-three curve

```
f(z) = z(z²−1)(z²−9)(z²+3) = z⁷−7z⁵−21z³+27z.
```

Its exact elliptic quotients are:

```
X₂=z+3/z,       Y₂=y/z²,
Y₂²=δ(X₂³−16X₂)       when y²=δ f(z);

X₃=z(z²−9)/(z²−1),   Y₃=y(z²+3)/(z²−1)²,
Y₃²=δ(X₃³+27X₃).
```

The rational automorphisms used in the computations are

```
(z,y) ↦ (3/z, 9y/z⁴),
(z,y) ↦ ((z−3)/(z+1), 16y/(z+1)⁴).
```

These identities alone imply neither existence nor nonexistence of the desired
quadratic divisor. Twists δ vary; ranks for one twist are not global bounds.

### New verified Lean file

`Submission/GenusThreeCurve.lean` is a standalone, hole-free 244-line file. It
proves the two quotient identities, the reciprocal identity, and the following
polynomial certificate:

```
V² − δ f = W² (X²+bX+c)
```

If `W` is nonzero at the five rational branch points and its evaluation at
`√−3` has nonzero norm, all six displayed quantities are rational squares.
The sixth assertion uses Mathlib's `QuadraticAlgebra ℚ (-3) 0` and its
multiplicative norm, rather than numerical complex calculations.

Main lemma names include:

```
degree_two_quotient
degree_three_quotient
pell_branch_square
pell_extra_square
pell_square_conditions
square_conditions_iff_norms
exists_nonreal_parameter
exists_template_parameter
```

The last lemma constructs a nonreal `t` with rational norms of
`t,t+1,t−1,t+2,2*t+1,t²+t+1`, from the six square conditions and `b²<4c`.
It does NOT claim that such b,c exist, nor that every such parameter is in
general position. Its `RationalNorm` is in its own namespace, not the namespace
of `QuadraticTemplate.lean`.

All printed dependencies are exactly `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`.
Log: `/tmp/genus_three_lean.log`.

### Symbolic Jacobian search

`genus3_jacobian_search.sage` uses the twist `δ=f(r)` over `ℚ(r)`, starting at
`P=(r,f(r))`. The six rational automorphism images give divisors `D_i=2[P_i−∞]`.
Their sum is exactly zero. Cantor arithmetic is performed in the genus-three
Jacobian; a reduced Mumford polynomial of degree two is a candidate for U.

- The initial sparse search (two or three nonzero coefficients, each ±1)
  had 100 distinct cases. All had generic degree three and no nonbranch
  rational specialization lowering the degree.
- `genus3_symbolic_box.sage` tests the five independent coefficients in
  `[-2,2]`, modulo global sign, with the sixth coefficient zero: 1562 cases.
  It examines every rational root of the denominators of the generic monic
  Mumford polynomial, excluding the branch values 0,±1,±3, then re-evaluates
  the group operation exactly at any such root. There are no such nonbranch
  rational roots in this box. The six generic degree-two cases are just the
  doubled rational curve points, whose quadratic has discriminant zero.

This is an exact bounded lattice search, not a proof about all Jacobian points,
all twists, or all rational-distance configurations.

/tmp/genus3_jacobian_search.log

/tmp/genus3_symbolic_box.log
```

### Fixed-twist elliptic-factor searches

The elliptic models used for a positive twist δ are

```
E₂: y²=x³−16δ²x,
E₃: y²=x³+27δ²x.
```

Rational points on E₂ pull back to quadratic divisors via
`U=z²−(x/δ)z+3`, `v=(y/δ)z² mod U`. A second copy is obtained with the order-three
automorphism. E₃ pulls back via
`U=z³−(x/δ)z²−9z+x/δ` and
`v=(y/δ)(z²−1)²/(z²+3) mod U`.
All polynomial congruences are checked exactly before creating the divisors.
Doubling these generators gives a subgroup of `2J(ℚ)`.

For δ=210, Sage gives ranks 2 and 1. A first coefficient-box test found no
quadratic divisors. `genus3_isogeny_cosets.sage` then expresses three times each
known doubled curve point in the five elliptic-factor generators. It uses a
finite-field meet-in-the-middle lookup ONLY to propose coefficients, followed
by exact equality checks over ℚ. The known orbit generates three cosets of the
elliptic-factor subgroup. Searching coefficients `[-2,2]` in these cosets tests
9375 group elements. Its only degree-two results are the six doubled rational
curve points (and their negatives), all of discriminant zero. No claim is made
that these are all cosets of the full Mordell–Weil group.

## Polynomial rigidity (verified)

`Submission/QuadraticRigidity.lean` now compiles in full. The four printed
axiom checks use only `propext`, `Classical.choice`, and `Quot.sound`.
Log: `/tmp/quadratic_rigidity_lean.log`.

The file first proves that a polynomial over any field which is a square in
its rational-function field was already a polynomial square. Over the reals,
this implies that the Gram polynomial for a quadratic path
`t² a + t b + c` cannot be a rational-function square unless `a,b` are
linearly dependent. Consequently a universal symbolic rational-distance
construction by a nondegenerate quadratic image of a line cannot work.

A stronger checked lemma is `two_anchor_polynomial_rigidity`: if real
polynomials x(t), y(t) pass through (0,0) at t=0 and both

```
x(t)²+y(t)²,
(x(t)−1)²+y(t)²
```

are squares in the rational-function field, then y is identically zero.
The proof makes their square roots polynomials r,s and uses Heron's identity

```
4 y² = ((r+s)²−1)(1−(r−s)²).
```
If both r+s and r−s were nonconstant, their absolute values would eventually
exceed 1, making the right side negative. Thus one is constant. Evaluation
at t=0 shows its square is 1, forcing y=0.

This theorem concerns SYMBOLIC square identities for a whole polynomial
path. It does not rule out rational square values at selected parameters,
does not apply to every rational (nonpolynomial) parametrization, and gives
no bound for arbitrary finite rational-distance configurations.

A reexamination of inversion gives no new growth mechanism. Inversion
preserves generalized circles (ordinary circles and lines). A set with four
points on one generalized circle still has four on a generalized circle
after inversion, unless one of those points is the center and is deleted.
In particular, a rational-distance set of n+1 points with no four on ANY
generalized circle would yield an n-point general-position set by inversion
at one of its points, but the required source sets have not been constructed.
Large line-or-circle examples do not satisfy this prerequisite. This is a
mathematical diagnostic, not a newly Lean-certified existence theorem.

`Submission/Spec.lean` remains unchanged: the general conjecture has its
original `sorry`, and the unconditional certified cases are n ≤ 7.

## Further extension diagnostics: orthogonal grids

The latest continuation reexamined doubling/reflection, polynomial motion,
and line-to-curve transformations. None supplies an unconditional growth
step. The existing symbolic catalog and square-factor experiments must not be
mistaken for a classification of all possible extensions.

A precise orthogonal specialization would require rational u != 0 with
both u²+1 and u²+4 rational squares. If these squares are v²,w², then

```
X = u², Y = u*v*w,
Y² = X*(X+1)*(X+4).
```

Sage's exact rank computation for `EllipticCurve([0,5,0,4,0])` gives rank zero,
label 24a1, and the full rational torsion list

```
O, (-4,0), (-2,±2), (-1,0), (0,0), (2,±6).
```

The only nonnegative x values are 0 and 2; 2 is not a rational square, so this
computation excludes nonzero u for that specialization. This is NOT currently
Lean-certified and is NOT used as a theorem in any submission file. The
2-isogenous model is y²=x(x−1)(x−9); it too has a certified rank-zero Sage
descent. This conductor-24 calculation should not be confused with the older
conductor-48 isosceles-median specialization.

One possible formal proof would use elementary 2-isogeny descent: for
E with (A,B)=(5,4), the x square classes are supported on ±1,±2. For the
2-isogenous E' with (A',B')=(−10,9), positivity and a mod-9 obstruction
eliminate the nontrivial candidate class 3. Turning this into the rational
point classification also requires a genuine height descent or equivalent
Mordell–Weil argument; that last step has NOT been proved here. Do not assert
rank zero in Lean based solely on the Sage output.

The main statement is still unresolved, and `Submission/Spec.lean` has not
been changed or submitted as a completed proof in this continuation.

## Lean-certified local part of the orthogonal descent

`Submission/OrthogonalDescent.lean` is now a hole-free auxiliary file. It has

Verified results:

- `quartic_three_dvd`: if integers a,b,c satisfy
  `c²=3a⁴−10a²b²+3b⁴`, then 3 divides both a and b. This follows from an
  exhaustive modulo-nine calculation using kernel-checked `decide`.
- `quartic_not_square`: for EVERY rational u, `3u⁴−10u²+3` is not a rational
  square. The proof clears denominators, uses `Rat.isSquare_intCast_iff`,
  applies the preceding divisibility lemma, and contradicts coprimality of
  u's numerator and denominator.
- `curve_point`: the simultaneous conditions `v²=u²+1`, `w²=u²+4` yield

- `isogenous_curve_point`: for u != 0, the explicit image

These local and algebraic lemmas DO NOT prove the full rank-zero statement.
A global height descent (or an equivalent Mordell–Weil argument) is still

there are no nonzero u with both u²+1 and u²+4 squares without supplying that
additional argument. There are local solutions of the latter conditions near
u=0, so it is not a purely local obstruction.

## Nondegenerate median fibers do not make the extra square automatic

This continuation returned to a possible construction mechanism, rather than
expanding a finite search. The question was whether the extra eighth-template
norm might become a square identically on a suitable rational-median elliptic
fiber. That mechanism is now ruled out for the following entire fibration.

For rational A,B with A²=2B²−1, put c=A*a+B (the second side is normalized to 1).
One doubled median is automatically 2B*a+A. The other two squared medians are

```
Q1(a)=(2−A²)a²−2AB*a+2−B²,
Q2(a)=(−1+2A²)a²+4AB*a+2+2B².
```

The extra square is

```
D(a)=a⁴+1+(A*a+B)⁴−a²−a²(A*a+B)²−(A*a+B)².
```

### Exact symbolic diagnostic

`median_fibration_squareclass.sage` computes discriminants and resultants in
the rational parameter

```
A=(k²+4k+2)/(k²−2), B=−(k²+2k+2)/(k²−2).
```

The only rational exceptional parameters in those calculations are −2,−1,0.
Each makes c=±a±1, a degenerate triangle; the parameter at infinity is likewise
degenerate. The computations completed (an initial JSON-serialization error
was fixed and the script rerun successfully):

```
/tmp/median_fibration_squareclass.log
/tmp/median_fibration_squareclass.json
```

This is an exact exceptional-parameter calculation, not a bounded height scan.
Its rational-root classification is not itself imported into Lean.

### Stronger Lean-certified obstruction

`Submission/MedianFibration.lean` (about 420 lines) now proves
`no_automatic_extra_square`: if A,B are rational, A²=2B²−1, and B² != 1,
then D is NOT a square in

```
Q(a)(sqrt(Q1(a)), sqrt(Q2(a))).
```

The field is represented by nested `QuadraticAlgebra`s. Its construction and
all required non-square statements are checked, not assumed from Sage.
The file is hole-free, has only `import FormalConjecturesUtil`, and all printed
axiom checks use only `propext`, `Classical.choice`, and `Quot.sound`.
Log: `/tmp/median_fibration_lean.log`.

Proof ingredients:

1. A base-field element d becomes a square after adjoining sqrt(q) exactly
   when d or q*d was a base-field square. Applying this twice gives the four
   square classes D, Q1*D, Q2*D, Q1*Q2*D.
2. `extra_squarefree` proves D squarefree. An explicit polynomial Bezout
   certificate for D and D' has nonzero constant
   `6*(B²−1)*(B⁴−8B²+4)²`. Vanishing of the last factor would give a rational
   square root of 3. The certificate was generated by Sage but its polynomial
   identity is proved by `ring` in Lean.
3. D has degree 4. Squarefreeness excludes the first three square classes,
   because Q1 and Q2 have degree at most 2.
4. `extra_positive` proves D(a)>0 for every real a. Its only possible real
   zero would have a²=c²=1 and a rational doubled median with square 3.
5. `exists_negative_median_product` proves Q1(a)*Q2(a)<0 somewhere on the real
   line. Otherwise both quadratics would be everywhere nonnegative (their
   sum is a²+c²+4>0). Their discriminants are respectively
   `24*(B²−1)` and `−24*(B²−1)`, forcing B²=1. Consequently Q1*Q2*D cannot
   be a square either.
6. `ruling_relation`, `ruling_degenerate_iff`, `ruling_nondegenerate`, and
   `ruling_median_identity` check the k parametrization and its exact three
   finite degenerate parameters.

`Submission/BiquadraticSquares.lean` separately preserves the small generic
square-class lemmas, also verified with the permitted axioms.

Certificate-generation artifacts:

```

/tmp/median_fibration_bezout.sobj

### Limits of this result

This is a FUNCTION-FIELD obstruction to an automatic construction. It does NOT
exclude square values of D at individual rational points of a fiber. It does
not classify rational-median triangles, prove the conditional eight-point
surface has no rational points, or give any universal cardinality bound.
There is still no unconditional eight-point example or arbitrary-size
construction. `Submission/Spec.lean` is unchanged and its original main
`sorry` remains. No completed proof was submitted.

On the generic twist delta=f(r), the six automorphism orbit points define

Vnew=Y*((8*t^2-27)/(27*t^2)*x^2-4/(3*t)*x-3/t^2).
```

### Exact mixed-factor theta calculation

The general-Y E3 translated formula is now verified by exact polynomial
remainder, not only at Y=1. `genus3_E3_translate.sage` gives the quotient and
checks all five real square-class ratios (`/tmp/genus3_E3_translate.log`).

`genus3_mixed_theta.sage` combines the translated E3 divisor with the true
E2 pullback class, represented by U2=x*(x^2-s*x+3), V2=w*x^2 (the quadratic
fiber class alone differs from the group-homomorphic pullback by T0).
Normalize Y3=1 and delta=1/(t^3+27t), so w^2=(s^3-16s)/(t^3+27t).
The generic degree-three sum has coordinate denominators t*(t-9s/4)^2.
At t=9s/4, exact recomputation gives a degree-two divisor. Put q=27w/8;
its coefficients simplify to

```
b=-8/(s*(1-q)), c=3*(1+q)/(1-q),
q^2=3*(s^2-16)/(3*s^2+16),
b^2=4c/(3+q^2).
```

For real |s|>4 this would have negative discriminant. But rational s,w on
this specialization are already obstructed by a rank-zero genus-one curve.
The quartic 3*(s^2-16)*(3*s^2+16) transforms via h=1/(s-4) to

```
v^2=1536*h^3+768*h^2+144*h+9.
```

Its elliptic model has minimal model y^2=x^3+6x-7, conductor 72, rank zero;
Sage's torsion list yields only s=+/-4 and the points at infinity. This
rational-point classification has NOT been formalized in Lean.

Independently, imposing the five real square characters would require, with
r=4/s, the three squares 1+r, 1-r, 1+r^2/3. They map to

```
E: y^2=x*(x+3)*(x-9), x=-3r^2, y=9r*u*v*w.
```

Sage computes conductor 72, rank zero, and only full two-torsion. Again this
is a computational diagnostic, not a Lean theorem or a conjecture disproof.
Scripts and logs: `genus3_mixed_{theta,specialize,obstruction}.sage` and
`/tmp/genus3_mixed_{theta,specialize,obstruction}.log`.
All 32 rational branch-torsion translates of the mixed calculation are now
being inspected by `genus3_mixed_torsion.sage`.

`genus3_mixed_torsion.sage` completed all 32 translates in 336 seconds. Every

## Three-saturation: the missing cosets can now be reconstructed exactly

The independent rank scan completed all 306 squarefree delta <=500 in 368s.
It certified 117 twists with both elliptic ranks positive (99 rank-3, 5 rank-4,
7 rank-5, 6 rank-6 Jacobians). Other twists are explicitly marked unfinished
where Sage could not certify generators; there is no classification claim.

expressions, with no quadratics. It skipped large generators and timed out
one factorization. This result is superseded as a search restriction below.

### Factoring was unnecessary for real-character kernels

`genus3_independent.sage` now computes the kernel by Gray-code enumeration of
products of the five character values, using exact integer square tests.
No integer factorization is needed. Homomorphism controls test square ratios.
This changed delta=71 from a 180-second factorization timeout to a 0.17-second
exact search. The earlier factoring version is preserved separately.

### Exact finite-field 3-divisibility filter

`genus3_saturation_filter.sage` tests which coefficient vectors modulo 3 could
be divisible by 3 in J(Q). For each good prime below 600, it constructs the
ENTIRE 3-primary subgroup of J(Fp), generated from rational curve points,
and checks its cardinality against the elliptic-factor order formula. A
prime is skipped if that construction does not reach the full cardinality.
It then computes J(Fp)/3J(Fp) explicitly and intersects the resulting linear
kernels over F3. These are necessary conditions only, not rational lifts.

As a control, delta=210 leaves precisely the known vector (1,2,2,1,2),
matching the independently verified curve-orbit preimage. Independent twists
also have nontrivial kernels, e.g.

```
delta=5:   (1,2,1)
delta=65:  (1,2,0,0,1,1), (0,0,1,2,2,1)
delta=78:  (1,2,2,1).
```

The batch `genus3_saturation_runner.py` finished all 112 remaining selected
twists in 166 seconds; the five initial/control cases were run separately.
Logs and exact matrices: `/tmp/genus3_saturation_<delta>.{json,log}`.

### Rational reconstruction and exact verification

`genus3_divide_three.sage` uses good primes with 3 not dividing #J(Fp), where
three-division is unique. It takes the inverse of 3 modulo #J(Fp), then uses
CRT and rational reconstruction on the Mumford coordinates. EVERY accepted
rational divisor is checked both on the curve and by the exact equation
3D=target in J(Q). Thus no reconstruction or height heuristic is accepted
as a proof of existence by itself.

For delta=5, the missing division class was recovered after five primes:

```
U=x^3-4/5*x^2-33/5*x-49/5,

It satisfies 3D=2*(G0-G1+G2), for the old undoubled factor generators.
Both independent missing classes for delta=65 were recovered after 10 and
15 primes. The known delta=210 case was recovered independently as a control.

The search basis is enlarged without increasing its rank: if 3D=2H, then
E=2D-H satisfies 3E=H and replaces the pivot old generator. The new

### Lean-certified elliptic-quotient obstructions

`Submission/QuotientObstructions.lean` is a new hole-free, 199-line standalone
file with only `import FormalConjecturesUtil`. All axiom checks use only
propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. Log:
`/tmp/quotient_obstructions_lean.log`.

For nonreal z with rational norms of z,z+/-1,z+/-3, put

```
X2=z+3/z,
X3=z*(z^2-9)/(z^2-1).
```

The file proves:

* X2 is nonreal: Im(X2)=Im(z)*(1-3/|z|^2), and |z|^2=3 would contradict
  rationality of |z|.
* X3 is nonreal, using the exact identity
  X3=z-4/(z-1)-4/(z+1). Its imaginary part has the sign of Im(z).
* |X2-4| and |X2+4| are rational, from their factorizations
  (z-1)(z-3)/z and (z+1)(z+3)/z.
* |X3| is rational, from z(z-3)(z+3)/((z-1)(z+1)).
* normSq(X2) != -16 and normSq(X2+/-4) != 32; normSq(X3) != 27.
* `normSq_of_conjugate_involution` verifies that
  conj(w)=e+k/(w-e), for real e,k and w != e, forces |w-e|^2=k.
* `quotientTwo_no_trivial_conjugacy` excludes
  conj(X2)=X2, -16/X2, 4+32/(X2-4), -4+32/(X2+4).
* `quotientThree_no_trivial_conjugacy` excludes
  conj(X3)=X3 or 27/X3.

These are the x-coordinate patterns for identity or rational two-torsion
traces on the two elliptic quotient curves. The coordinate exclusions are
formalized, but their interpretation using the elliptic-curve group law and
a classification of all rational torsion have not been formalized here.
In particular no elliptic rank theorem or cardinality bound is being asserted.

`median_elliptic_lift.sage` now searches the Mordell-Weil lattice of the

```

     +158436r^4-55404r^2+6561.

Put u=r^2+9/r^2. Its quotient quartic is

```
v^2=P(u)=u^4-76u^3+1920u^2+29360u+31984.
```

Writing A=-38, B=238, L=47448, M=-24660 gives
P(u)=(u^2+A*u+B)^2+L*u+M. The birational elliptic model is

```

X=-2*(v-u^2-A*u-B), Y=-2X*u-A*X-L.
```

For X != 0 the inverse is u=(Y+L+A*X)/(-2X).
The exceptional point (0,-L) gives u=-M/L, whose square is <36 and thus
has no real r; (0,+L) and infinity are the infinite quartic fibers.
The returned rank-three generators are

```

```

## Threefold-rotational orbit equations (verified, existence unresolved)

`Submission/ThreefoldOrbits.lean` gives exact arithmetic for two orbits of
rotation by a cube root of unity in characteristic 3. Normalize the first
orbit representative to sqrt(-3), whose orbit has side length 3. The
second representative is x+y*sqrt(-3). Its squared orbit side is
3*(x^2+3*y^2), and the three cross squared lengths are

```
x^2+3*(y-1)^2,
(x+3/2)^2+3*(y+1/2)^2,
(x-3/2)^2+3*(y+1/2)^2.
```

Writing their square roots as a,b,c and the second orbit side as s gives
the exactly equivalent equations

```
a^2+b^2+c^2=s^2+9,
a^4+b^4+c^4-a^2*b^2-a^2*c^2-b^2*c^2=9*s^2.
```

The inverse coordinates are x=(b^2-c^2)/6 and
y=(b^2+c^2-2*a^2)/18. Both directions are proved in Lean.
`equal_cross_degenerate` proves that a^2=b^2 forces c=0, s^2=9,
and a^2=9; it cannot produce two distinct general-position orbits.
`common_circle_control` verifies the degenerate rational family
a=6v,b=3(v-u),c=3(u+v),u^2+3v^2=1,s=3.
All four axiom checks use only the allowed axioms. Verification log:
`/tmp/threefold_orbits_lean.log`. No nondegenerate pair is asserted.

The exact integer diagnostic `threefold_exact.cpp` tests the equivalent
un-normalized equations S=a^2+b^2 and Delta=a^2*b^2, where a,b are orbit
sides and S,Delta are computed from the three cross lengths. Delta must
be a square d^2, and S+2d and S-2d must be squares of a+b and a-b.
It uses three modular filters and fully checked integer square roots.
It excludes equal orbit radii (common circle) and repeated cross lengths
(the proved degeneracy). A bound-2000 run has been started. Any later
positive arithmetic result still needs full general-position checks.

The original Spec.lean conjecture remains unchanged and unresolved.

## Cubic-fiber / isotropic-quadric construction (new structural route)

This is a NEW restricted construction, not a solution or an obstruction for
arbitrary rational-distance sets. The original Spec.lean remains unchanged.

### Exact distance identity, verified in Lean

`Submission/CubicFiber.lean` establishes a polynomial identity over every
commutative ring. For parameters a,b,c,d,k define

```
PX(x,y)=y^2-x^2-4ay+4cx,
PY(x,y)=-2xy-2by+2dx,
F(x,y)=x(x^2+y^2)-2a(x^2-y^2)-2bxy-2kx-(b^2+4a^2)y,
G(x,y)=y(x^2+y^2)-2c(x^2-y^2)-2dxy+(d^2+4c^2)x
       -2(k+4ac+bd)y,
S(x,y,u,v)=u^2+v^2-x^2-y^2+2xv-2yu.
```

Then

```
(PX(x,y)-PX(u,v))^2+(PY(x,y)-PY(u,v))^2
 = S(x,y,u,v)^2
   +4(x-u)(G(x,y)-G(u,v))-4(y-v)(F(x,y)-F(u,v)).
```

Consequently rational points in one common fiber of (F,G) have rational
mutual distances after the map (PX,PY), explicitly abs(S). Theorems:
`distance_identity`, `same_fiber_distance_sq`, `point_dist`,
`point_rational_distance`, `fiber_pairwise_rational`.
The distance and rationality theorems have compiled with only the allowed
axioms; `/tmp/cubic_fiber_lean.log` is the current compilation log.

The file also checks the symmetric subfamily a=c=1,b=d=u:
m=(u^2+4)/2, k=m(m-2)/2 gives

```
G-F=(y-x)(x^2+y^2-m^2).
```

Thus its zero fiber splits into a diagonal branch and a circle branch.
The quadratic image of the diagonal is collinear. This is NOT a general
cardinality bound. The last tiny fix to the split lemma (`0-0=0`) is being
compiled at this log entry; poll the log before claiming its final axiom check.

Lean implementation detail: because PX,PY,S are generic over a ring, the
cast must explicitly specify the inner rational type, e.g.
`((signedChord x y u v : ℚ) : ℝ)`. Merely specifying the outer ℝ causes
Lean to instantiate the generic function at ℝ and coerce its arguments.
The `ℝ²` notation also needs `open EuclideanGeometry`.

### Origin of the identity

This route uses the symplectic pairing on four coordinates and its square
on the ten-dimensional space of symmetric tensors. The real signature
of the latter is (4,6), NOT the initially guessed (6,4). A totally isotropic
three-space of quadrics leads to a four-dimensional quotient of signature
(1,3), giving the Euclidean distance construction. In a normalized chart,
three quadrics are

```
qx=t*x+a(x^2-y^2)+b*x*y+k*x*z+(b^2/2+2a^2)*y*z+A*z^2,
qy=t*y+c(x^2-y^2)+d*x*y-(d^2/2+2c^2)*x*z
   +(k+4ac+bd)*y*z+B*z^2,
qz=t*z+(x^2+y^2)/2.
```

intersection points (the usual Bezout bound), so this particular model
is not an arbitrary-cardinality mechanism. No Lean formalization of that
Bezout assertion or of a complete classification of positive-dimensional
fibers has been made. Do NOT use it as a bound on arbitrary configurations.

## Elliptic-octad continuation: torsion obstruction and a non-torsion test

The conjecture in Spec.lean is still unchanged and unresolved.

### Finite torsion-group certificates (fully verified)

`Submission/TorsionOctads.lean` proves, for each of

```
Z/8, Z/9, Z/10, Z/12,
Z/2 x Z/4, Z/2 x Z/6, Z/2 x Z/8,
```

that every eight-element subset whose sum is zero contains a four-element
subset whose sum is zero. `split_subset` extracts the subset statement
from the computable `OctadsSplit` predicate. All seven certificates use
ordinary kernel `decide`; all nine printed axiom checks pass with only the
permitted axioms. The file does NOT prove or invoke Mazur's torsion theorem,
and it does NOT formalize the elliptic-curve/projective geometric link.

The motivating standard geometry is the degree-four embedding of an elliptic
curve by |4O|: four points are coplanar when their sum is O; eight points are
a quadric divisor when their sum is O. Consequently torsion-only zero-sum
octads in the listed groups cannot avoid coplanar quadruples. This is only
an obstruction to that proposed construction, not to arbitrary distance sets.

Exact finite counts (`torsion_octads.py`, `/tmp/torsion_octads.json`):
zero-sum octads number 0,1,5,43,1,45,818 in the order above. None avoids a
zero-sum quadruple.

The same Lean file proves a counterexample in the infinite cyclic group:

```
{-8,-7,-6,2,3,4,5,7}
```

has eight distinct integers, sum zero, and no four-element zero-sum subset.
Thus the torsion calculation must not be promoted to a statement about all
rational points of an elliptic curve.

## Unit-vector cube diagnostic (new construction, no witness)

A different possible eight-point template is the set of all subset sums of
three unit vectors u,v,w in the plane. Normalize u=(1,0), and choose v,w as
squares of rational Gaussian unit vectors. Explicitly, for t=a/b,

```
v(t) = ((b^4-6*a^2*b^2+a^4), 4*a*b*(b^2-a^2))/(a^2+b^2)^2.
```

Then all distances involving differences supported on at most two of u,v,w
are rational. The remaining conditions are exactly the four squares

```
|u+v+w|^2, |u+v-w|^2, |u-v+w|^2, |u-v-w|^2.
```

There is no generic geometric degeneracy: `planar_cube.sage` checks exactly
that u=(1,0), v=(-7/25,24/25), w=(-119/169,120/169) give eight subset sums
with no collinear triple and no concyclic quadruple. However, their four
body-diagonal squares are 28417/4225, 333/845, 8833/4225, 2357/845; these
are not all rational squares. This is NOT an integral-distance example.

`unit_cube_search.cpp` implements an exact bounded search, using modular
quadratic-residue bitset filters and GMP perfect-square checks. It checks
all primitive a/b with 0<a<b<=B. Modulo primes congruent to 3 mod 4 the
coordinate denominators are always invertible, so the sieve can safely use
the reduced unit vectors. The four tested residues for a pair (x,y),(z,w) are
3+2*s*x+2*t*z+2*s*t*(x*z+y*w), for s,t in {+1,-1}.

At B=10000, there are 30,397,485 primitive fractions. The individual modular
obstructions leave 256,097 unit vectors. The pairwise filters at
7,19,11,23,31,43,47,59,67,71,79,83,103,107,127,131 leave 202 pairs for exact
GMP tests. None satisfies all four square conditions, even before imposing
general position. Runtime was about 12 seconds. Artifacts:

* `/tmp/planar_cube.log`
* `/tmp/unit_cube_search_10000.log`
* `/tmp/unit_cube_results_10000.txt` (empty)

The earlier B=500 run also found no pair. These are bounded arithmetic
searches, not a classification of rational unit cubes or of arbitrary
rational-distance sets. No Lean theorem has been claimed from these C++/Sage
computations. This template itself only targets eight points, not all n.

The relaxed subset-sum cube has source vectors u,v,w with thirteen required

u,v have the six rational norms |u|,|v|,|u+v|,|u-v|,|2u+v|,|u+2v| from the
median construction. It has only seven distinct vertices, with collinearities,

`cube_geometry.sage` factors all triangle/circle determinants of the eight

removing the common nonzero y factor, are a,b,a±1,b±1,a±b,a±b±1. There are 46
distinct circle-determinant factors (including some triangle factors).
No determinant factor vanishes identically on a=1+t,b=1-t. Thus this particular
unfolding of the collision is not forced to remain geometrically degenerate.

it still requires EIGHT quadratic polynomials in t to be rational squares.

Y^2 = X^3 + 9*(k^2+2*k+2)^2*X^2
            - 576*k^2*(k+1)^2*(k+2)^2*X.

Sage verifies an exact isomorphism with the quartic obtained from the existing

G1 = (-12*k*(k+1)*(k+2),

G2 = (-8*k^2, -8*k^2*(9*k^2+26*k+18)).
```

All sixteen relations are verified as exact equalities in E(Q(k)) by

### Fast enumeration of centrally symmetric configurations

`search_central.cpp` searches sets `{+/-u,+/-v,+/-w,+/-z}` with maximal radius
`|u|=a`, other radii positive integers less than a, and integral lengths to
both anchor points +/-u. Other pair distances may be rational before the
final scaling by a. Equal radii are excluded because two antipodal pairs of
equal radius are cocircular.

For a candidate of radius b, if its two anchor lengths are c,d, then

```
c^2+d^2 = 2*(a^2+b^2).
```

Writing c=e+f and d=e-f gives an integer sum-of-two-squares representation
`e^2+f^2=a^2+b^2`. The relevant nondegenerate representations have e>a and
0<=f<b. Scaled coordinates are

```
x=e*f,
y*sqrt(D)=sqrt(a^2*b^2-e^2*f^2),
H=(a-f)*(a+f)*(b-f)*(b+f), D=squarefree_part(H).
```

The code factors all a^2+b^2 by a modular-root sieve and enumerates all their
Gaussian representations. It checks both |v-w| and |v+w| before searching
for compatible triples. Exact 128-bit norm and 256-bit determinant bounds
are safe through its maximum supported radius 2,000,000.

An independent brute-force anchor-length reference agreed on 117 cases
(a=2..40, targets 4,6,8); log `/tmp/test_central.log`. The radius-2523 six-point
control recovered characteristic 2002 and passed the independent verifier.

### Reflection extension: exact restricted algebraic obstruction

`central_seven_reflection.sage` examines the normalized quadratic seven-point
template above. It checks all 105 ways of choosing a singleton and partitioning
the other six into three pairs having the same sum. The potential eighth point
is the reflection of the singleton about that common center. Each ideal is
saturated by the original pair differences and all new-point differences, to
exclude coincident points.

49 matchings have no remaining complex solutions. The other 56 have
zero-dimensional ideals. `central_seven_reflection_arithmetic.sage` eliminates
w and obtains 28 distinct cubics in t; every one is irreducible, witnessed
already modulo 3 or 5. There are no linear/quadratic factors.

For a rational-distance source normalized at u=1, both Re(t) and |t|^2 are
rational (use the lengths of t and 1-t), so t has degree at most two over Q.
Consequently none of these noncoincident reflection candidates can come from
such a source. This rules out THIS PARTICULAR seven-to-eight reflection
mechanism. It is an exact Sage-based calculation, NOT a Lean-certified theorem,
and does not classify arbitrary seven-point sets or arbitrary extensions.

### A different fibration and a new Lean-verified restricted obstruction

For side lengths a,b,c, the extra square is U=-2a^2+6b^2+3c^2.
A useful fibration sets c=alpha*a+beta*b with beta^2=3alpha^2-2. Then

```
U=(beta*a+3alpha*b)^2
```

identically. With b=1, the remaining three median polynomials are

```
f0(t)=2t^2+2-(alpha*t+beta)^2,
f1(t)=2t^2-1+2(alpha*t+beta)^2,
f2(t)=-t^2+2+2(alpha*t+beta)^2.
```

The rational conic parametrization is

```
alpha=(k^2+2k+3)/(k^2-3), beta=(k^2+6k+3)/(k^2-3).
```

The three quadratic discriminants are respectively
32(alpha^2-1), -40(alpha^2-1), and 8(alpha^2-1).
The three pairwise quadratic resultants, after imposing the conic relation, are

```
Res(f0,f1)=(7beta^2-4)^2+24beta^2+48,
Res(f0,f2)=25beta^4+52beta^2+4,
Res(f1,f2)=16beta^4+16beta^2+49.
```

All are strictly positive for real alpha,beta. Thus no two polynomials share
a complex root. The only repeated-branch case is alpha^2=1, which forces
alpha,beta in {+1,-1}; the resulting side relation has zero Heron polynomial.
Consequently this particular fibration does not acquire a nondegenerate
low-genus fiber by branch collisions. The genus interpretation itself has NOT
been formalized; the discriminant identities, positivity, disjoint complex
roots, and zero-Heron exception HAVE been formalized.

## Squared-Mobius norm closure and a Pythagorean central template (NOT SOLVED)

### A new verified anchor construction

Even powers of arbitrary polynomial factors have rational norm in an imaginary
quadratic field. This motivates going beyond the fixed finite factor supports
of the earlier S-unit catalogs (some of which already allowed even powers of
an extra factor, but still had a prescribed support).

For g in C, define F(g)=4g^2/(1+g^2)^2. Then, away from the denominator zero,

```
1-F(g)=((1-g^2)/(1+g^2))^2,
F(g)-F(h)=4(g-h)(g+h)(1-gh)(1+gh)/((1+g^2)^2(1+h^2)^2).
```

`Submission/SquareMap.lean` (83 lines) proves these identities and proves
rational distances from F(x+y*sqrt(-D)) to anchors 0 and 1 for rational x,y
and natural D, whenever the denominator is nonzero. It is hole-free, and all
three printed axiom checks use only the permitted axioms.
Compilation: `lake env lean -j 1 Submission/SquareMap.lean`.
Log: `/tmp/square_map_lean.log`.
This is an anchor-construction tool, not an eight-point existence theorem.

### New conditional eight-point template (Sage arithmetic; no witness)

The complex Pythagorean specialization

```
u=1+t^2, v=2t, w=1-t^2, so u^2=v^2+w^2,
```

makes a fixed point of one generic involution equal to v*w. Inverting there,
including the image of infinity, and clearing the common complex denominator
produces these eight polynomial points:

```
0,
(1/2)*(t^2+1)*(t^2+2t-1),
t*(t^2+1),
(1/2)*(t-1)*(t+1)*(t^2+1),
(1/2)*(t-1)*t*(t^2+2t-1),
(1/2)*(t-1)*(t^2+1),
(1/2)*t*(t+1)*(t^2+1),
(1/2)*(t+1)*(t^2+2t-1).
```

Every one of their 28 differences factors into rational constants and

```
t, t-1, t+1, t^2+1, t^2-2t-1, t^2+2t-1.
```

Thus rational norms of these six factors suffice for rational pair distances.
General position is NOT automatic for every parameter. An exact geometric
test at t=17/29+(11/31)*sqrt(-2) found no collinear triple or concyclic quadruple,
showing that the determinant polynomials are not identically zero. This test
parameter does NOT satisfy the rational norm hypotheses and is NOT an
Erdos witness. The template has not been formalized in Lean.

## Square-area descent and complete pencil coverage (NOT SOLVED)

The pending proof in `PythagoreanFibration.lean` has been repaired and verified,
as recorded above. Two new auxiliary files now prove that its omitted symmetry
loci cannot contain a positive-area admissible parameter.

### Fermat's square-area theorem (Lean verified)

`Submission/FermatArea.lean` gives a self-contained descent proof of:

```
no_rational_square_area:
  0<x -> 0<y -> 0<z -> x^2+y^2=z^2 -> not IsSquare(x*y/2)
quartic_not_square:
  t != 0 -> not IsSquare(t^4+6*t^2+1)
```

The first theorem uses strong induction on the integer hypotenuse after clearing
rational denominators and reducing to a primitive Pythagorean triple. In the
primitive classification x=m^2-n^2, y=2mn, coprimality and square area make m,n,
m+n,m-n squares. Square roots of m+n and m-n give a smaller square-area right
triangle. The quartic theorem uses the legs

```
abs(c)+(t^2-1), abs(c)-(t^2-1)
```

and hypotenuse 2(t^2+1) when c^2=t^4+6t^2+1; its area is (2t)^2.
This is a proved classical auxiliary theorem, not a new solution of Erdős 213.
All four printed axiom checks pass with only the allowed axioms.
Log: `/tmp/fermat_area_lean.log`.

### All positive-area norm parameters lie in the pencil (Lean verified)

`Submission/PythagoreanCoverage.lean` imports the two auxiliary modules. It proves:

* `trace_ne_zero`: s>0 and all six norm squares imply x!=0. Setting x=0 and
  s=a^2 would require the forbidden quartic a^4+6a^2+1 to be a square.
* `unit_norm_excluded`: x^2<s and all six norm squares imply s!=1. Apply
  the verified Mobius rotation; s=1 gives zero transformed trace and a
  strictly positive transformed norm.
* `admissible_fibration_covers`: every x^2<s parameter satisfying all six
  square conditions has r!=0, 1-r^2!=0, and x=r*(1-s)/(1-r^2).
* Negation and inversion preserve the six square conditions; inversion
  transforms area into (s-x^2)/s^2.

Compilation log: `/tmp/pythagorean_coverage_lean.log`. All four printed axiom
checks use only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. For the auxiliary imports,
compiled objects were generated at `.lake/build/lib/lean/Submission/` using:

```
lake env lean -j 1 -o .lake/build/lib/lean/Submission/FermatArea.olean Submission/FermatArea.lean
lake env lean -j 1 -o .lake/build/lib/lean/Submission/PythagoreanFibration.olean Submission/PythagoreanFibration.lean
lake env lean -j 1 Submission/PythagoreanCoverage.lean
```

Do not import these into Spec.lean in a final submission; its original import
must remain unchanged, and any needed auxiliary proof must be inlined there.

Neither a new unconditional cardinality nor a global bound was proved. The
strongest certified case remains all n<=7, and Spec.lean still contains the

## Normalized spiral route (NOT SOLVED)

A new route was investigated with the aim of reducing arbitrary finite sizes
to one family. It has NOT supplied admissible parameters of arbitrary length.
The strongest unconditional cardinality in Spec.lean remains seven.

### Correct normalization and Lean-verified distance criterion

Define P_k(z)=1+z+...+z^(k-1), with P_0=0. Then

```
P_(m+n)-P_m=z^m*P_n,
dist(P_(m+n),P_m)=|z|^m*|P_n|.
```

For n>=3, all distances among P_0,...,P_(n-1) are rational if and only if
|z| and |P_k| (0<=k<n) are rational. Importantly, |1-z| is NOT required:
normalization of the first edge removes that extra, unnecessary constraint.
`Submission/Spiral.lean` proves these identities and the equivalence, as well
as the norm formulas below and a five-point seed's rational distances. All
five printed axiom checks use only the allowed axioms. Log:
`/tmp/spiral_lean.log`.

For x=Re(z), s=|z|^2,

```
N(P_2)=s+2x+1,
N(P_3)=s^2-s+1+2x(s+1)+4x^2,
N(P_4)=(s+2x+1)*((s-1)^2+4x^2).
```

Writing s=a^2 and N(P_2)=b^2 gives x=(b^2-a^2-1)/2 and

```
N(P_3)=a^4-a^2*b^2+b^4-a^2-b^2+1.
```

The family b=a^2/2 makes this a square identically:
N(P_3)=(a^4/4-a^2/2+1)^2. It does not make the subsequent norms automatic.

### Exact geometry and section calculations (Sage)

`spiral_norms.sage` reduces P_0,...,P_8 modulo z^2-2xz+s and computes their
norms. It factors all 56 triangle and 70 circle determinants for the first
eight points. There are 42 distinct factors; none of the determinants is
identically zero. Every circle determinant has a factor s-1. Examples of
triangle degeneracy factors are 2x+1, 2x+s, and x.
Log/data: `/tmp/spiral_norms.{log,sobj}`.

A development error in printing cyclotomic norms was corrected: direct
coercion `T(cyclotomic_polynomial(k))` put its variable into the coefficient
ring. The corrected code uses `T(list(cyclotomic_polynomial(k)))`. The P_k
norm and determinant calculations were unaffected; the current cyclotomic
output is correct.

`spiral_sections.sage` interpolates quadratics through the rational boundary
points of the quartic model. It finds 18 nondegenerate rational-function
sections, of degrees 1 through 7. Their additional Phi_4 norm square classes
have degrees 8 through 28, not zero. These are exact identities, not a
classification of all rational points.
Artifacts: `/tmp/spiral_sections.{log,sobj}`.

## Monomial-direction route (NOT SOLVED)

The conjecture remains unchanged, with its sole main sorry. This route supplies
no eight-point witness and no global upper bound. The newest unconditional
cardinality theorem is still n<=7.

### Exact symbolic graph and unbounded exponent patterns

Over Q(t), with involution t -> 1/t, let u=epsilon*t^a, v=delta*t^b and
F(u,v)=(1-v)/(u-v). Then F*=uF and (F-1)*=v(F-1). For a second point (U,V),

```
F(u,v)-F(U,V)=(U-u+v-V-vU+Vu)/((u-v)(U-V)).
```

The connecting phase is a signed monomial exactly when the numerator is
reciprocal or anti-reciprocal up to a monomial shift.

`monomial_direction_graph.py` constructs this graph using exact Laurent
coefficient dictionaries. At exponent bound 5 it has 420 vertices and 1230
edges; at bound 12 it has 2352 vertices and 9240 edges. Neither graph has a
five-point general-position configuration including anchors 0 and 1.
These are bounded graphs, not a theorem about arbitrary exponents or points.
Logs/data: `/tmp/monomial_direction_{5,12}_5.{log,json}`.

`test_monomial_direction.sage` independently checks every eligible pair in the
bound-5 graph (including nonedges) by direct rational-function arithmetic.
It obtains exactly the same graph. It also specializes one four-point example
at t=((3+4i)/5)^2 and checks rational distances and general position exactly.
Log: `/tmp/test_monomial_direction.log`.

`monomial_direction_classify.sage` then removes the exponent bound. It expands
the twelve-term signed coefficient identity through all 6! positive/negative
term matchings, using exact rational row spaces in a,b,c,d,L. After excluding
forced anchor degeneracies, ten of the sixteen sign patterns each have six
maximal edge spaces; six have none. All 60 spaces have reciprocal sign -1.
`monomial_five_classify.sage` combines these spaces for three non-anchor
vertices: 22 compatible sign-color triples, 216 choices each, 4752 systems.
Every system forces a listed GP degeneracy. It supplies exact rational linear
combination certificates for all 4752 systems.

Artifacts: `/tmp/monomial_direction_classify.log`,
`/tmp/monomial_edge_spaces.{sobj,json}`, `/tmp/monomial_five_classify.log`,
`/tmp/monomial_five_cert.{sobj,json}`.

A tempting shortcut is INVALID: matching only the original three positive
and three negative terms misses cancellation spaces in nine sign cases.
`monomial_matching_control.sage` detects this. The full 6! calculation, not
that shortcut, is the classification being used.

## Circumcenters and spiral-center closure (NOT SOLVED)

This continuation did not settle the conjecture. Spec.lean is unchanged, with
its original main sorry, and the unconditional cardinality result is still
n<=7. The following two new Lean files compile completely with only the three
permitted axioms. All catalog nonexistence results below are exact finite
Python/Sage computations, not Lean theorems about arbitrary configurations.

### Scaled shared-edge circumcenters (Lean verified)

`Submission/CircumcenterScale.lean` proves Lagrange's identity and its rational
square consequence. If

```
u^2+D*v^2=r^2, r!=0, u*s+D*v*t=0,
```

then D*(s^2+D*t^2) is a rational square, with square root
D*(u*t-v*s)/r. Subtracting two perpendicular-bisector equations gives the
orthogonality hypothesis.

The geometric theorem `shared_bisectors_rational_distance` embeds rational
coordinates as x+y*sqrt(-D), with D natural. It proves that two centers on the
same perpendicular bisector have rational mutual distance after multiplying
both by sqrt(-D), provided the shared chord has nonzero rational length.
It does not claim that all circumcenters have rational mutual distances.
Log: `/tmp/circumcenter_scale_lean.log`.

`circumcenter_graph.py` constructs all 35 scaled triangle circumcenters for
each of the known characteristic-2002 and characteristic-77 seven-point sets.
Every center is checked against its three defining squared distances.

| characteristic | vertices | rational-distance edges | edges from shared chords | extra edges | maximum GP subset in this catalog |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2002 | 35 | 245 | 210 | 35 | 4 |
| 77 | 35 | 240 | 210 | 30 | 4 |

For example, centers of triangles (0,1,2) and (0,3,4) have nonsquare scaled
distance norm in both sources. Thus the common scaling does NOT turn all
35 centers into a rational-distance set. An independent quadratic-field
all-pairs check agrees with both graphs.
Artifacts: `/tmp/circumcenter_graph_{2002,77}.{log,json}` and
`/tmp/test_circumcenter_miquel.log`.

### Spiral-center extension and seven-term completion (Lean verified)

`Submission/SpiralCenter.lean` defines

```
m(a,b,c,d)=(a*c-b*d)/(a+c-b-d).
```

Away from its denominator zero, it proves the four exact difference identities
and, in particular,

```
dist(m,a)=dist(a,b)*dist(a,d)/norm(a+c-b-d).
```

The analogous formulas hold for b,c,d. Four rational edge lengths and a
rational denominator norm therefore imply four new rational distances.
Conversely, if a!=b,d and those two original lengths are rational, one new
rational distance already forces the denominator norm to be rational.
The denominator is twice the distance between the appropriate diagonal
midpoints (the 'bimedian' condition).

It also proves the three pairwise difference identities for the three spiral
centers of a quadrilateral. For example, with
k1=a+c-b-d, k2=a+b-c-d, k3=a+d-b-c,

```
m(a,b,c,d)-m(a,c,b,d)=-(a-d)*(b-c)*k3/(k1*k2).
```

Consequently `rational_seven` proves that a rational quadrilateral with all
three nonzero rational bimedians yields the seven-term rational-distance list

```
a,b,c,d,m(a,b,c,d),m(a,c,b,d),m(a,b,d,c).
```

That theorem does not assert injectivity or GP. No general GP growth claim
should be inferred from it. All three printed axiom checks pass.
Log: `/tmp/spiral_center_lean.log`. The only initial proof error was a remaining
nonzero-product division in the converse, fixed by simplifying with that
product's nonvanishing.

### Finite spiral-center closure

`miquel_closure.py` applies the rule to every GP rational-distance quadruple in
the current finite pool, testing all three pairings. Only nonzero rational
bimedians are accepted. Exact Fraction arithmetic records each new point's
four parents. The name 'miquel' here is just the development script name;
the proved formulas, not an unproved circle interpretation, justify the rule.

Starting with characteristic 2002, successive pool sizes are

```
7 -> 14 -> 68 -> 263 -> 1461 -> 18009.
```

At the fifth round, 333423 quadruple partitions are tested, 56133 have square
bimedians, and 16548 distinct new points are added. The saved homogeneous
integer coordinates have at most 84 bits. The characteristic-77 source is
already closed under this operation on its seven points: nine pairings have
rational bimedians, all returning old points.

At three rounds, the 263-point pool has 2866 rational-distance edges and a
maximum GP subset of size seven. The first naive five-round all-pairs Fraction
run timed out after generating 18009 points; it did NOT finish its graph check.
The script was changed to save the point/provenance checkpoint before that
phase, and the graph was then checked by the exact method below.

`rational_point_sieve.cpp` implements a necessary-condition modular sieve for
rational coordinates. At any prime dividing a coordinate denominator it skips
that test, so such primes never reject a valid edge. The Python driver uses
25 primes and independently checks every surviving squared integer norm by
integer isqrt. The C++ size guards keep its modular arithmetic within 64 bits.

`miquel_graph_sieve.py` then computes the seven-core and performs an exact GP
clique search. The initial ordering recomputed degrees too expensively and
was stopped; the final implementation uses a fixed degeneracy ordering and
bounded determinant caches. Neither the arithmetic tests nor the search's
mathematical scope changed.

For the 18009-point pool:

* 756620 modular survivors;
* 756606 exact rational-distance edges (14 false sieve hits rejected);
* seven-core: 17996 vertices, 756528 edges;
* graph degeneracy: 56;
* no GP eight-clique, after 1865250 search nodes;
* total final sieve/search runtime about 19 seconds.

These results concern this five-round pool ONLY, not its infinite closure or
all integral-distance sets. A seven-point witness is present, so the maximum
GP cardinality in this finite pool is seven. Intermediate 'best reached'
prints in target-eight searches are not independently maximum claims.

Artifacts: `/tmp/miquel_generation_2002_{2,3,5}.log`,
`/tmp/miquel_points_2002_{2,3,5}.json`,
`/tmp/miquel_closure_{2002,77}_3.{log,json}`,
`/tmp/miquel_sieve_2002_{2,3,5}.{log,json,graph.json}`.
The `.bin` and `.pairs` files retain the modular input and survivors.

### Generic heptad factor audit (Sage, not Lean)

A useful model for the seven-term completion, after normalizing three vectors,
is the generic list

```
1+v+w, 1-v-w, -1+v-w, -1-v+w, -v*w, -w/v, -v/w.
```

Its pair distances are rational if the norms of
v,w,1+/-v,1+/-w,v+/-w are rational. These are hypotheses, not automatically
satisfied at the symbolic GP test points.

`spiral_heptad_factors.sage` studies all 105 spiral-center pairings from this
list over Q(v,w), factoring all seven new differences. Factors in the eight
known linear supports are removed, as are even powers. The remaining formal
square-class incidence matrix has rank three or four in the nondegenerate
cases. This is formal factor rank, NOT a proof of independence of specialized
arithmetic norm classes or a necessary number of arithmetic constraints.

The initial exact GP specialization v=2+3i,w=-4+5i accidentally made eleven
otherwise nondegenerate candidates fail GP. It was NOT used as a universal
obstruction. `spiral_heptad_degeneracies.sage` independently tested constant
ratios/cross-ratios over Q(v,w), revealing the mistake. The final specialization
v=17+29i,w=-31+43i avoids all those accidents. Final exact classification:

* 9 pairings return old points;
* 12 have a forced real cross-ratio equal to 2 with three old points;
* 84 give GP eight-tuples at the final exact specialization;
* of those 84, 36 have formal extra-factor rank three and 48 rank four.

The twelve forced cross-ratio identities are saved as exact rational-function

## Discriminant-first median surface (NOT SOLVED)

The previous continuation introduced a different fibration but did not append
it to this log. Normalize the middle squared side to 1 and write the other
squared sides as A,C. The doubled-median squares are

```
2A+2-C, 2A-1+2C, -A+2+2C.
```

The extra discriminant is Delta=A^2+1+C^2-A-AC-C. Its squarehood is completely
parametrized by rational s,q:

```
A=1+q(s^2-1), C=1+q(2s-1), Delta=q^2(s^2-s+1)^2.
H=2A+2C+2AC-A^2-1-C^2=(1+qs^2)(3-q(s-2)^2).
```

`median_discriminant_surface.sage` verifies these identities and constructs
two elliptic quotients over Q(s). Its log and saved models are
`/tmp/median_discriminant_surface.log` and
`/tmp/median_discriminant_quotients.sobj`.

Put L=s^2+2s-2, R=s^2-s+1 and, for q nonzero, T=1/q+L/3. Define

```
a1=(2s^2-2s-1)/3, a2=(-s^2+4s-1)/3, a3=-L/3, h=2R/3.
```

Then a1+a2+a3=0, sum ai^2=2R^2/3, and

```
A=q(T+a1), C=q(T+a2), 1=q(T+a3),
M3=3q(T-a1), M1=3q(T-a2), M2=3q(T-a3),
H=3q^2(T^2-h^2).
```

The median involution fixes s and sends q to -3q/(3+2qL), hence T to -T.
All five remaining square conditions imply a point on

```
Y^2=3 product_i (T^2-ai^2).
```

Its two elliptic quotients are Y^2=3 product(X-ai^2) and
Z^2=3 product(1-ai^2 X). Their generic j-invariants are unequal and
nonconstant; none of the three rational degree-2 isogenies of the first
quotient has the second j-invariant, and the first has no rational
3-isogeny. This is not a proof of nonisogeny at every degree.

Both q=-1/s^2 and q=3/(s-2)^2 give the five squares, but have H=0.
They are not admissible witnesses. Individual square conditions are stronger
than membership on the genus-two curve or either elliptic quotient.

An isosceles diagnostic gives the curve y^2=x(x+1)(x+9), Cremona 48a3,
rank zero and torsion Z/4 x Z/2 according to Sage. This is not a Lean proof
of an isosceles obstruction. Log: `/tmp/median_isosceles_rank.log`.

`median_genus_two_sections.sage` exploits the possible shared roots of the
