    (2vt-v^2m-2vm-m)(2vt-v^2m+2vm-m)(2t-vm)^2.

The first two roots are real for unit v; the double root is vm/2. This is
why the direct square-root calculation did NOT cover reflected candidates.

For a mirrored control pair P(u,1),P(1/u,1), normalize the candidate's scale
m>0 and Im u,Im v>0. The redundancy P(-v,-m)=P(v,m), conjugation of the
candidate, and interchange of the mirrored controls permit this normalization
without restricting the quartic template. All unit parameters are non-axis.

For the opposite edge

    E=t-P(v,m)-P(1/u,1),

the homogeneous quartic discriminant has three essential factors: two
squared small factors and one large factor f. The small factors are exactly
nonzero multiples of

    H_{1/u}(m v),   H_v(1/(u m)),
    H_w(z)=z^2-(2w+1/w)z+w^2-1.

They cannot vanish: the two evaluation points lie in the wrong half-planes
for the previously proved stable-root restriction. The elimination of f and
its unit-circle conjugate has the exact resultant

  4096 (v-u)^4(u+v)^4(v-1)^8(v+1)^8(u-1)^8(u+1)^8 v^16 u^16
    [128u^8+11827u^6v^2+299523u^4v^4+11827u^2v^6+128v^8]^2.

The kernel-checked norm bound excludes the final bracket. Thus v=+-u;
positive imaginary parts exclude v=-u. Substituting v=u leaves

    f(u,u,m)=u^9 F(u^2+u^-2,m).

For unit u, z=u^2+u^-2 is real and <=2. The kernel-checked positive
factorization of F excludes this last case. Hence the opposite edge has
nonzero homogeneous discriminant and is squarefree. Degree drop from four
to three is covered: when the quartic coefficient is zero, this discriminant
is the square of the cubic leading coefficient times the cubic discriminant;
if degree drops further the homogeneous discriminant is zero.

Consequently square norm of this opposite edge forces a fixed complex
direction. No assumption of distinct initial exterior positions is needed,
thanks to `squarefree_norm_all_directions`.

### Radial reflected branches and the leading-degree-drop warning

Full exact saturation of the four leading-coefficient phase equations on

    u*v*m*(u^2-1)*(v^2-1) != 0

gives the necessary scale relation

    (m^2-1)(m^3+uv)=0.

Unit u,v and real positive m force m=1. At m=1 the phase equations force

    (v-u)(uv+1)=0.

At m=-1 the corresponding formula is (v+u)(uv-1)=0; this is redundant after
positive-scale normalization but was checked independently as well.

* v=u is the exact midpoint-reflection candidate t-P(u,1), excluded by the
  new all-degree Lean theorem.
* v=-1/u is NOT automatically radial: its fourth coefficient vanishes, so
  all fourth-pivot phase equations are vacuous. This degree-drop branch must
  be checked using its actual cubic coefficients. Here

      E=(4+8/u^2)t^3+(2/u^4-1/u^2)t,

  and the first/third coefficient phase is

      -8u^-4(u-1)(u+1)(u^2+1)(u^4+(3/2)u^2+1).

  Thus, excluding the axis parameters, radiality requires u^2+1=0 or
  2u^4+3u^2+2=0. In these cases the norm to the OTHER control is respectively

      16t^8-24t^6+9t^4-t^2+1,
      14t^8-10t^6+(41/16)t^4-(17/32)t^2+343/2048.

  Both are squarefree octics. The two exact Lean Bezout certificates above
  establish the corresponding nonsquareness (the second after constant
  scaling). No reflected candidate survives the two-edge conditions.

family against this mirrored QUARTIC control, with independently checked

## Genus-two reciprocal field obstruction and exact metric audit (MAIN NOT SOLVED)

Continued the common-field investigation from the split genus-two control.
It produces a new complete restricted obstruction, NOT an arbitrary point-set
bound, a GP8 witness, or a settlement of Erdős 213.

### Concrete control: all conjugate choices fail even up to similarity

The four nonreal quadratic representatives have discriminants

  -4, -1175/9216, -47/144, -1175/16.

The three in Q(sqrt(-47)) have upper roots

  A=(19+5sqrt(-47))/192,
  B=(23+sqrt(-47))/24,
  C=(19+5sqrt(-47))/8.

Their same-sign squared distances are exactly

  AB²=3/4, AC²=529/24, BC²=18.

Thus a common quadratic field does not even give a rational triangle, and
no common nonzero real scale repairs this triangle. Moreover, conjugating
any selection of the roots does not repair it. Up to conjugating all three,
fix the sign of A positive. The BC²/AB² ratios for signs (B,C) are

  (+,+): 24
  (+,-): 1099/36
  (-,+): 24
  (-,-): 20736/1099.

All four are nonsquares in Q. If one common nonzero scale made both incident
edge lengths rational, that ratio would be the square of their rational
quotient. The general ratio lemma and all four exclusions are Lean-proved.
This is a specific finite control, not a classification of all genus-two
representatives or all point sets.

For completeness, the six pairwise resultants of the four U polynomials,
ordered as in the source JSON ([]; [4]; [0,1]; [2,3]), are

  8825/9216, 529/144, 8825/16, 1099/1536, 566559/1024, 3297/8.

Only the second is a rational square. A nonsquare resultant alone does NOT
exclude one selected upper-root distance: it is the product of the two
squared conjugate distances. The explicit edge-ratio argument above avoids
that invalid inference.

Taking both conjugates of many representatives is independently blocked
by the existing reflection-pair geometry: two complete conjugate pairs
are concyclic if their real parts differ, and collinear otherwise. No
new general-position growth mechanism was obtained from the torsion coset.

### Entire reciprocal subfamily: modulo-three obstruction

The control belongs to the rational reciprocal family

  F=2X(X²-r²)(X²-r^(-2)),
  U=X²+1, V=(r+r^(-1))(X+1), r!=0.

For translation by the two negative reciprocal branch roots, put

  T=(X+r)(X+r^(-1)),
  W=-(r+X)(X-1)(rX+1)/r,
  E=X²+(r+r^(-1)-4)X+1.

Exact polynomial identities are

  W=V mod U, T divides W,
  F-W²=-U*T*E,
  -disc(E)=((r-1)/r)²*(6r-r²-1).

The factor identity and discriminant identity are kernel-checked in Lean.
The CRT interpretation is also independently checked in Sympy. No general
Jacobian-to-Euclidean-distance correspondence is assumed.

If the branch distances from i are rational, r²+1 must be a rational square.
But r²+1 and 6r-r²-1 cannot simultaneously be rational squares for ANY
r in Q, including zero. Clear only the primitive denominator of r. Rational
squares that are integers have integer square roots, giving

  A²=p²+q²,
  B²=6pq-p²-q²,

with coprime integers p,q. Modulo 3, A²+B²=0 forces A=B=0 mod 3; the first
equation then forces p=q=0 mod 3, contradicting coprimality. This is an
unconditional local obstruction, not a finite-height search or a heuristic
elliptic-rank calculation. If r=1 the branch condition already fails since
2 is not a rational square; otherwise the displayed nonzero square factor
shows that -disc(E) cannot be a rational square. Thus this translated
quadratic cannot align with the source imaginary field Q(i) while retaining
the rational branch distances.

This excludes the displayed reciprocal subfamily, not the general
independent-two-parameter genus-two family, unions of different fibers, or
arbitrary rational-distance configurations.

NEW COMPLETE file: Submission/UnitCubeNormalForm.lean (228 lines), sole
import FormalConjecturesUtil. It supplies a completeness theorem for the

### Characteristic and complete normal form

For rational D,x,y,a,b with y!=0,

 x²+D*y²=1,
 (1+x)²+D*y²=a²,
 (1-x)²+D*y²=b²

imply IsSquare D, with explicit square root a*b/(2*y). Thus the equal-edge
planar cube cannot escape the rational Cartesian-coordinate model by using
a nonsquare characteristic, provided the two face lengths are rational.
This is a restriction on the equal-edge model, not on arbitrary integral
point sets with unequal distances.

Define for rational t

 vx(t)=(1-6t²+t⁴)/(1+t²)²,
 vy(t)=4t(1-t²)/(1+t²)²,
 point(t)=vx(t)+i*vy(t).

complete_normal_form proves that every complex z with norm one, positive
imaginary part, and rational norms of 1+z and 1-z is point(t) for some
rational 0<t<1. complete_up_to_sign covers either nonreal half-plane, giving
z=point(t) or z=-point(t).

The proof takes p=norm(1+z)/2 and q=norm(1-z)/2, as rational numbers. Then
p,q>0, p²+q²=1, Re(z)=p²-q², Im(z)=2pq in the upper half-plane. The inverse
parameter is t=q/(1+p). Both inequalities and both coordinate identities
are proved, not assumed from a parametrization chart. Independent sign
changes of generators translate/relabel cube vertices. Rotation and common
scale normalize the first generator to one; those geometric operations are
used in the explanatory interpretation, not asserted as a new end-to-end
cube-to-conjecture theorem in this file.

### Automatic faces and remaining body conditions

Kernel-checked identities for all rational t,s are

 vx(t)²+vy(t)²=1,
 |point(t)+point(s)|²=
   [2*((1-t²)*(1-s²)+4ts)/((1+t²)*(1+s²))]²,
 |point(t)-point(s)|²=
   [4*(t-s)*(1+ts)/((1+t²)*(1+s²))]².

Taking s=0 also handles faces involving the normalized first generator one.
All edge and face norms are therefore rational. The four residual squared
body lengths are exactly

 body(t,s,e,f)=(1+e*vx(t)+f*vx(s))²+(e*vy(t)+f*vy(s))²,
 e,f in {1,-1}.

body_norm_iff proves equivalence of each rational-norm requirement and its
IsSquare condition, via a general norm_rational_iff for rational Cartesian
coordinates. It does not provide simultaneous square values. The old
geometric control t=1/2,s=2/3 is kernel-checked to fail the all-plus body
condition, whose squared length is 2357/845. This is an old control, not a
new candidate search or a global exclusion.

### Small complex-quadratic certificates

For A in C set

 f_A(X)=(A+1)(1-X²)+2i(1-A)X,
 N_A=f_A * coefficient_conjugate(f_A).

The Lean file proves the division-free Bezout identity

Hence f_A and f_B are coprime whenever A!=B. A second checked certificate is

 -4(A+1) f_A + [2(A+1)X-2i(1-A)] f'_A =-16A.

It proves squarefreeness whenever A!=0, including the linear degree-drop
case A=-1. For A!=-1 the polynomial has degree two. No resultant computation
is trusted by these proofs.

For A!=0, coefficient conjugation gives

 conjugate(f_A)=conjugate(A) * f_(1/conjugate(A)).

Consequently N_A is squarefree if A*conjugate(A)!=1. For nonzero A,B, it is
coprime to N_B if A!=B and A*conjugate(B)!=1. The conjugate reciprocal cases
are included explicitly, not omitted as generic exceptions.

### Uniform application to the four body lengths

Let x,y be rational, x²+y²=1, y!=0, and z=x+i*y. The four A parameters are

 1+z, -(1+z), 1-z, -(1-z).

They are pairwise distinct, nonzero, and different from -1. None has squared
norm one: that would give x=+-1/2 and (2y)²=3, contradicting rational
nonsquareness of three. The cross reciprocal coincidences also cannot occur.
These statements are all kernel-checked, using rationality and the unit
identity. Therefore the four N_A are all squarefree quartics and pairwise
coprime, for EVERY such rational x,y.

normBranch_eval supplies the actual metric bridge, for rational s:

 N_A(s)=(1+s²)² * norm(A+point(s))².

Its proof first checks

defining unrelated quartics.

nonempty_product_not_square proves every nonempty product of DISTINCT body
polynomials nonsquare: pairwise coprimality gives squarefreeness, while the
degree is exactly four times the number of selected factors. A squarefree
square would be a unit, contradicting positive degree. Integral closure of
C[X] in C(X) transfers this to the rational-function field.

class-independent elements of ANY characteristic-zero field. Repeated use

`Submission/CartesianGridMetric.lean` (153 lines) defines Grid A B for rational

It proves the iff with actual rational Euclidean distances in the complex

not a finite search or a bound on the cardinality of progression-free sets.

 (952-1800)^2+(960-1785)^2=1399729,

### A uniform geometric covering theorem

`Submission/CartesianGridCover.lean` (155 lines) proves `not_covered`:
for ANY finite real coordinate sets A,B with both cardinalities >2k, their
Cartesian product cannot be covered by k generalized circles (lines allowed).
No metric assumption, genericity assumption, or exclusion of vertical lines
is used.

For each covering set select its nonzero polynomial

 a(X^2+Y^2)+bX+cY+d.

The product over the covering family is nonzero over R and has degree at most
2k in each variable. If the family covered A times B, the product would vanish
on that entire grid. Mathlib's kernel-checked multivariate grid interpolation
(`MvPolynomial.eq_zero_of_eval_zero_at_prod_finset`) then makes the product
zero, a contradiction. The empty covering family and degenerate line factors
are included. Nonzero circle polynomials are certified using evaluation at
(0,0),(1,0),(-1,0),(0,1), not by an unchecked coefficient oracle.

The exact metric bridge to the conjecture's Euclidean plane is proved.
`erdos213For_of_grid` gives Erdos213For n when a rational-distance grid has
both coordinate cardinalities >2*(n+n^3), using CircleCoverReduction's
existing extraction/inversion/scaling theorem. Consequently
`conjecture_of_unbounded_grids` proves that unbounded rational-distance grids
would imply the original conjecture. This is SUFFICIENT ONLY, not an
equivalence and not an existence theorem for those grids.

No unbounded family of grids has been constructed. Even the weaker data of

As a mathematical warning (NOT a Lean theorem or an unconditional bound),
fixing three distinct horizontal coordinates of an all-distance grid and one
vertical coordinate puts every other vertical difference t on the simultaneous

and genus five by Riemann--Hurwitz. Thus arbitrarily large balanced grids
would in particular yield genus-five curves over Q with arbitrarily many
rational points. No uniform rational-point theorem is assumed or proved here.
This further illustrates that grid existence is a substantial missing premise,
not something established by the geometric extraction.

### Unrestricted formal lifting and arbitrary finite jets

`Submission/FormalDeformation.lean` (213 lines) is complete, warning-free, and
has an installed current olean. Nine printed axiom audits are permitted.

* `isSquare_of_constantCoeff_one`: every f in Q[[X]] with f(0)=1 has a square
  root in Q[[X]]. The proof substitutes f-1 in the binomial series with exponent
  1/2 and uses its exact multiplication identity.
* `isSquare_of_constantCoeff_square`: the same holds if f(0)=a^2 with a!=0.
* `collinear_deformation_squares`: for ANY family x_i,y_i of rational formal
  series with x_i(0)=a_i, y_i(0)=0 and distinct a_i, every pairwise norm
  (x_i-x_j)^2+(y_i-y_j)^2 is a square series. There is no degree/jet bound.
* `square_jets`: each square series has a polynomial square root modulo X^N
  for every N; the polynomial has degree <N. Its square need not equal the
  series beyond that jet.
* `arbitrary_formal_configurations`: the points (i+1, X*(i+1)^2), indexed by
  Fin n, have distinct formal x-coordinates, square norms, nonzero triangle
  determinants, and nonzero four-point circle determinants for every n.
  The geometry here is stated by determinants in Q[[X]], not as real metric
  predicates. The general factorization lemmas work over any commutative ring.
* `rational_specialization_iff`: for n>=4, all distances in this particular
  parabola family are rational at a rational parameter t iff t=0.

The last result uses only the edges with parabola parameters (1,2) and (2,4):

  d12^2 = 1+9t^2,
  d24^2 = 4+144t^2.

Dividing by (3t)^2 and (6t)^2 would make u^2+1 and u^2+4 square for
u=1/(3t), contradicting the completed OrthogonalGlobal descent. The statement
alone concerns rational t and unscaled distances, not all real parameters or
all similarity factors. The next file closes those two gaps for an explicit
six-point control, not for arbitrary configurations.

### Full distance equations: a nonsingular minor, not a parametrization

`Submission/DistanceJacobian.lean` (80 lines) is complete, warning-free, with
an installed olean and three permitted-axiom audits. For an arbitrary finite
edge set E, vertex set V, endpoint maps s,t, and variables x_v,y_v,d_e, it uses

  F_e=(x_s-x_t)^2+(y_s-y_t)^2-d_e^2.

The length-variable derivative matrix is exactly diag(-2*d_e), so its
determinant is nonzero whenever all d_e are nonzero. This includes every
collinear rational configuration with distinct endpoints, taking signed
lengths d_e=a_s-a_t. The equations and the determinant are both checked.

No scheme-theoretic smoothness wrapper, rational parametrization, Hasse
principle, or density theorem is asserted. In particular nonsingularity of
this minor supplies no implication that formal roots can be simultaneously

## Median-iteration obstruction for the oblique-grid completion (MAIN NOT SOLVED)

Revisited the oblique 3-by-3 grid without assuming the missing direction norms
or using the rectangular-grid obstruction. The eight-direction requirement
was already identified in the first GridTemplate investigation. The new result

GP8, weak9, or arbitrary-cardinality construction was obtained.

### Complete normal form for median iteration

`Submission/MedianFlipClosure.lean` is complete, warning-free, with installed
olean. Six printed axiom checks use only the permitted axioms.

For rational squared sides x=(A,B,C), define

  H(x)=(A+B+C)^2-2(A^2+B^2+C^2),
  M(x)=(2B+2C-A, 2A+2C-B, 2A+2B-C),
  R(x)=(A,B,2A+2B-C),
  scale(r,x)=r^2*x.

M gives squared lengths of the doubled medians; R switches the diagonal of a
parallelogram while retaining its two side lengths. The kernel-checked identities
are

  M(M(x))=9*x,
  H(M(x))=9*H(x),
  H(R(x))=H(x),
  H(scale(r,x))=r^4*H(x).

M commutes with side permutations and rational scaling. The inductive `Reach`
predicate permits arbitrary finite words in these three operations. The theorem
`reach_normal_form` puts every reachable triple into one of two forms:

  scale(r, x composed with p),
  scale(r, M(x) composed with p),

for rational r and a permutation p. There is no degree, parameter, or word-length
cutoff. `reach_preserves` verifies that rational sides and rational medians are
indeed preserved by all these operations. The zero scaling case is included in
the definition and does not escape the later nondegeneracy argument.

`flip_not_reachable` proves that when H(x)!=0 and both the sides and medians of
x have rational lengths, R(x) is NOT in this orbit.

* If R(x)=scale(r,M(x) composed with p), the Heron invariant gives 9r^4=1.
  Then 3r^2=1 would make 3 a rational square, impossible.
* If R(x)=scale(r,x composed with p), the same invariant gives r^2=1.
  Comparing the sums of the squared sides gives C=A+B.
* A nondegenerate right triangle cannot have all rational medians: after
  dividing by a nonzero leg, its hypotenuse and one doubled median would make
  u^2+1 and u^2+4 rational squares for nonzero u. This uses the previously
  completed OrthogonalGlobal descent, not a new unproved classification.

This is a restriction on a particular arithmetic-preserving orbit, NOT a
classification of all rational-median triangles or of all integral point sets.
In particular two unrelated rational-median triangles may lie outside each
other's orbit; no nonexistence of such pairs is claimed.

## Grid-center circular-cubic counterexample audit (MAIN NOT SOLVED)

The proposed unrestricted auxiliary premise that every integral-distance set
lies on a circular cubic is false. This does not refute Erdős 213.

Take the grid {0,364,418,782} x {0,240} and its center (391,120).
All nine points have integral pairwise distances. Cross-row horizontal
differences are 0,54,364,418,782, with corresponding distances
240,246,436,482,818. Center distances are 123 or 409.

For the eight points obtained by omitting (782,240), an independent SymPy
calculation checked all 28 squared distances using integer square roots and
computed the exact evaluation matrix in the basis

  x(x^2+y^2), y(x^2+y^2), x^2, xy, y^2, x, y, 1.

Its determinant is

  -1598908039506336977337817497600000,

and its rank over Q is eight. The coordinates, complete integer distance
matrix, rank, and determinant are recorded in

  /tmp/grid_center_circular_cubic.json.

An elementary verification: four roots on y=0 force the restricted cubic
to vanish. The circular cubic then has the form

  y [b(x^2+y^2) + d*x + e*y + f].

Three roots on y=240 force b=d=0 and f=-240e. Its value at (391,120)
then forces e=0. Thus no nonzero member of this polynomial space vanishes
on all eight points. This argument has not been Lean-formalized.

Scope and growth review: the full grid has four collinear points in each
row and concyclic rectangles. It is also contained in two concentric circles
of radii 123 and 409 together with their common center. Consequently this
seed provides neither a weak9/GP8 witness nor an unbounded generalized-circle
covering number. Inversion preserves such bounded generalized-circle covers.
No growth mechanism follows from the rank-eight calculation.

The preceding circular_cubic_diagnostic.py runs tested the stored finite
catalogs modulo 1000003. No rank-eight hit occurred in those catalogs; that
negative modular diagnostic was not an exact rank bound or a classification.
The explicit grid-center example above supersedes the unrestricted premise.

## Fixed-grid integer-extension completeness and independent audit (MAIN NOT SOLVED)

`grid_center_integral_extensions.py` completely enumerates integer-distance
extensions of the FIXED UNSCALED grid-center set, with no coordinate cutoff.
Take anchor distances a=364,b=240 and anchors O=(0,0),A=(a,0),B=(0,b).

  C=b^2(a^2-k^2)^2+a^2(b^2-l^2)^2.

## Quartic F4 anchor-orbit exhaustion (EXTERNAL, MAIN NOT SOLVED)

Rather than build a175501-vertex quartic graph, this investigation fixes two
outputs as anchors and uses exact root symmetries. It finds no GP8 in this
quartic root-product construction at the fixed grid. This is not a claim
about arbitrary rational-distance extensions.

### A coefficient-ratio lemma (mathematical argument, not Lean-formalized)

Let the root forms be nonzero linear forms with integer coefficients in
{0,+/-1}, and let P,Q,R be products of d such forms, representing distinct
projective product directions. If aP-bQ=cR with nonzero rational a,b,c, then

  b/a is +/-2^k for some -d<=k<=d.

Here is the argument, which is stronger than a finite ratio diagnostic.
Cancel the polynomial gcd of P,Q,R. By the displayed additive relation,
the remaining products P',Q',R' are pairwise coprime and have a common
positive degree e<=d. Choose a root factor H of R'. Eliminate one variable
using H=0; its coefficient is +/-1. Neither P' nor Q' becomes zero, since
neither is divisible by H. Every remaining root factor restricts to a
nonzero linear form with coefficients in {0,+/-1,+/-2}. In any monomial
order its leading coefficient is therefore +/-1 or +/-2. The two restricted
products have leading coefficients +/-2^u and +/-2^v, with 0<=u,v<=e.
Since a*P'=b*Q' after restriction, their ratio is +/-2^(u-v), as claimed.
Primitive normalization changes only signs: each original root is primitive
and a product of primitive integer polynomials is primitive.

This applies to both B4 and F4, and justifies the coefficient windows in the
quadratic/cubic catalogs after dividing by the smallest absolute coefficient.
For the new quartic search, translate one selected output to zero and scale
another to a primitive anchor product P. All other outputs are t*Q with

  t in +/-{1/16,1/8,1/4,1/2,1,2,4,8,16}.

A repeated product direction would give a collinear triple with zero, so
those candidates are legitimately excluded. Clearing the common denominator16
makes every coefficient-vector test integral. This argument is scoped to
GENERIC POLYNOMIAL FACTORIZATION identities with rational CONSTANT scalars;
it does not cover rational-function scalar coefficients or accidental squares
at specializations. It has not been kernel-verified.

## All-degree F4 coefficient normalization (Lean verified; MAIN NOT SOLVED)

The coefficient-ratio argument used in the preceding catalogs is now
kernel-verified. Two auxiliary files are complete, warning-free, and have

### Abstract specialization proof

`Submission/RootCoefficientBound.lean` (269 lines) defines SignedPowerTwo d q
and RatioBound d a b, where the latter means

  a*2^i = +/- b*2^j, with i,j<=d.

It proves the ratio bound from additive identities between equal-degree
products of factors, using a specialization for each factor. The relevant
specialization sends that factor to the outer variable X, and every other
factor to a polynomial with nonzero constant term. The inner-polynomial
leading coefficient of each trailing coefficient must be +/-1 or +/-2.

Equal multiset cardinalities and unequal multisets provide a factor with
strictly larger multiplicity on one side. The identity then forces the
lowest nonzero coefficients of the other two terms to cancel. Multiplicativity
of leading coefficients yields the bounded dyadic ratio. This avoids an
unformalized multivariate gcd/cancellation step and allows repeated factors.

Completed key statements include:

* trailing_relation
* ratio_bound_of_specializations
* multiset_eq_of_specializations
* ratio_bound_of_distinct_specializations
* normalized_dyadic_window
* RatioBound.signedPowerTwo_of_abs_le
* finite_family_normalization

The distinct-input version does not need a separate assumption that the
output direction differs from the first input. The additive identity and
nonzero scalar coefficients imply it. Proportional specialized products
have equal factor multisets, recovered from their orders of vanishing.

For a finite nonempty family of nonzero rational coefficients whose pairwise
ratios satisfy RatioBound d, finite_family_normalization chooses a coefficient
of minimum absolute value. After division by it, every coefficient is +/-2^k
with 0<=k<=d. This is the normalization used by the quadratic/cubic catalogs,
not an assumed bound on the original coefficients.

### Concrete F4 bridge

`Submission/F4CoefficientBound.lean` (252 lines) contains the exact24 root
coefficient rows of the F4 catalogs. Ordinary kernel decide verifies the
pivot and residue properties. With h a chosen root and p its pivot index,
the specialization uses

  x_p -> T - poly(h)(Z) + Z^p,
  x_i -> Z^i for i!=p.

Root h maps to T. Every other root maps to beta(Z)+c*T with beta nonzero
and all beta coefficients in {0,+/-1,+/-2}. Evaluation is implemented as an
MvPolynomial ring homomorphism, and the images of constants, roots, and
multiset products are proved explicitly.

The resulting coefficient_ratio and coefficient_ratio_of_distinct theorems
apply directly to an identity

  C(a)*rootProduct(s) - C(b)*rootProduct(t) = C(c)*rootProduct(u),

where s,t,u have common arbitrary degree d and a,b are nonzero rationals.
The latter theorem assumes only s!=t. rootProduct_direction_injective
proves uniqueness of product directions up to nonzero rational scalar.

family_coefficient_window combines this with minimum-absolute-value
normalization for any finite homogeneous product-difference family having
injective product directions. It does not claim that an arbitrary planar
integral configuration belongs to such a family.

quartic_coefficient_window gives precisely the anchored search window:

  if rootProduct(s)-C(b)*rootProduct(t)=C(c)*rootProduct(u),

## All-degree F4 S-unit identities and frame classification (EXTERNAL; MAIN NOT SOLVED)

This continuation replaces the degree-four cutoff by a structural necessary-
support enumeration. It obtains an externally audited classification of the
specified homogeneous F4 factor-supported rational-function construction.
It does NOT settle the original conjecture. No new Lean classification theorem
is claimed, and no eight-point arithmetic witness has been found.

### Mathematical completeness reduction (not yet Lean-formalized)

Let A,B,C be nonzero homogeneous products of distinct projective F4 root
forms, allowing repeated factors and nonzero rational scalar coefficients,
with A+B=C. Cancel their common gcd. The resulting products are pairwise
coprime and have a common positive degree d. Let m be the number of distinct
root forms occurring across the three products.

1. Color each used root by its product A,B,C; all unused roots have color0.
   In each rank-two flat, either at most one nonzero color occurs, or all
   three occur. A flat with exactly two colors is impossible: reducing the
   identity modulo the ideal of that codimension-two subspace forces a
   factor from the third product to lie in the same flat.

2. In a flat meeting all three colors, the sum of the exponents in each
   color is equal. To see this, use two transverse coordinates, with the
   remaining coordinates in a coefficient function field. If only one
   product had lowest order, its leading form could not cancel. If exactly
   two did, their leading forms would have to be proportional. They are
   products of disjoint sets of distinct linear forms, so cannot be
   proportional. Thus all three orders agree.

3. The homogeneous Mason--Stothers bound is d<=m-2. Choose one used root h,
   and a generic rational affine line u+t*v with h(v)=0 and h(u)!=0. Every
   other used root has a distinct finite zero on this line and nonzero
   leading coefficient. The two products not containing h still have degree
   d; all products stay nonzero and pairwise coprime. The radical of their
   product has degree m-1. Polynomial ABC gives d<=m-2. Existence of the
   generic rational choice follows by avoiding finitely many proper
   algebraic conditions over the infinite field Q. This homogeneous chart
   argument is a mathematical deduction, not a new Lean theorem; the older
   SUnitDegreeBound file proves the underlying univariate support bound.

Every nonconstant factor-supported rational function f for which 1-f is
also factor-supported reduces to such a primitive identity. Its numerator,
denominator, and complementary numerator have equal homogeneous degree.
Thus this reduction handles arbitrary integer exponents in rational
functions, not only a preselected polynomial degree. Rational CONSTANT
scalar coefficients are allowed; arbitrary non-factor-supported functions
and new linear factors are outside its scope.

## Broader linear-factor and square-factor growth review (MAIN NOT SOLVED)

Returned to the unrestricted constructive gap after the all-degree F4
classification. No new bounded catalog was launched, no new Lean theorem
was asserted, and no new configuration was obtained.

For a fixed nonreal normalized alpha in an imaginary quadratic field, the
allowed rational roots r with |alpha-r| rational form an infinite conic
supply. This supply is not itself a growth theorem. In fact every nonreal
point z=a+b*alpha with rational a,b and rational |z| already has the form

  z=b*(alpha-r), r=-a/b,

with an allowed root r. For two such points, if b_i!=b_j, rationality of their
distance is exactly the allowed-root condition at

  r_ij=-(a_i-a_j)/(b_i-b_j).

If b_i=b_j, their difference is rational real and its length is automatic.
Thus arbitrary allowed factors together with arbitrary rational constant
coefficients already re-encode the normalized original metric problem at
degree one. Taking all coefficients equal only places the points on one
line. Neither infinitude of the conic nor its rational parametrization
establishes simultaneous compatibility of the r_ij. This elementary
observation is mathematical reasoning here, not a newly claimed Lean theorem.

Also reviewed the existing square-factor map, its independent pair-difference
condition, and rational-function square-difference constructions. The
verified rational distances to two anchors do not make the remaining edges
automatic. No non-isotrivial arbitrary-cardinality square-difference family,
new elliptic lifting theorem, or distance-preserving extension rule was
obtained. The earlier finite square-factor tests are not a global exclusion.

## Exact degree-two extension analysis of the symmetric-six family (EXTERNAL; MAIN NOT SOLVED)

The six functions are
 F=[0,1,(t+3)/2,(t^2-9)/(t+1)^2,-(t-5)^2/(16(t-1)),2(t-3)/(t+1)^2].
Here t^2=-C and the allowed square classes are C+1,C+9,C+25. All tests below
are GENERIC over Q(C), not at just C=35581/900. They do not exclude accidental
arithmetic squares at any particular rational C, functions involving the input
square roots, or higher rational-map degrees.

The norm test always uses the FULL rational norm f(t)f(-t). In the reduced
norm numerator and denominator, replace t^(2k) by (-C)^k, multiply these two
polynomials, remove all powers of the three allowed branches, and test that
the remaining polynomial is a rational square. Checking only a reduced
numerator of f would be invalid because cancellation can change numerator
and denominator square classes separately; that earlier implementation issue
was repaired before the successful computations recorded here.

### Mathematical coverage wrapper (not a Lean theorem)

The following explains why these catalogs cover nonreal rational functions
of rational-map degree at most two under the GENERIC norm conditions. This
argument and the external enumerations have not been kernel-formalized.

Write f=A/B reduced, with deg A,deg B<=2, and C0=B-A. The three polynomials
A,B,C0 are pairwise coprime. Since N(A)/N(B) and N(C0)/N(B) have allowed square
classes, their norms have the same class modulo the allowed branches. At an
unsupported prime of Q(C), there are at most two conjugate primes above it
in Q(t). Three coprime polynomials cannot all have odd norm valuation there;
an inert prime has even norm valuation automatically. Hence each of the
three polynomial norms separately has only allowed odd branches. Its leading
coefficient as a polynomial in C is a rational square, so there is no missing
constant square class.

For a polynomial at most quadratic this means, up to rational scalar:
 E: it is even;
 S: it is a squared rational linear polynomial, including a constant;
 L: it is supported on the six allowed roots, with infinity representing a
    missing degree (thus constants and linears are also included).
For a quadratic a*t^2+b*t+c, its norm is
 a^2*C^2+(b^2-2ac)*C+c^2,
whose discriminant is b^2*(b^2-4ac). If b=0 it is E; if b^2=4ac it is S;
otherwise an allowed norm forces both roots to be allowed rational roots.
Linears are handled by their norm a^2*C+b^2. Constants are E and S.

If two of A,B,C0 are E, so is the third and f is real. Three distinct S forms
cannot give a primitive nonconstant identity: three distinct points of the
quadratic Veronese conic are not collinear. If at least two forms are L, the
finite catalog covers them (in the primitive case a supported complementary
root cannot also be a root of the denominator). A constant complement is
covered by cancellation of leading coefficients or by the even condition.

The remaining combinations are E/S/L, S/S/L, S/S/E. The first two yield
Families I and II above by cancellation of coefficients. Repeated L roots
reduce to S/S/E, opposite L roots reduce to E, and a constant L is E and S.
The finite/infinity formulas explicitly cover linear L forms. A constant S
in Family II with quadratic L is the limit u=infinity already checked.

For S/S/E, if one S form is constant, the other must be even, so f is real.
Otherwise their two squared linear roots u,v are finite and distinct. If
one is zero, cancellation of odd coefficients forces the other coefficient
to vanish or both forms even. Thus the nonreal primitive case has
u*v*(u-v)!=0. Cancelling odd coefficients gives exactly the two-parameter
family displayed above, up to one of the six transforms. This direct
polynomial argument covers degree drops without assuming that a compactified
parameter limit stays in an affine chart.

The external results and this wrapper therefore suggest the exact generic
nonreal degree<=2 extension list consists only of F2,F3,F4,F5 and G=(t-3)/2.
G has the stated forced circle. This is NOT a bound for arbitrary rational
functions, specialized arithmetic extensions, or configurations in Spec.lean.
No unrestricted conclusion is drawn from this classification argument.

### Explicit cubic families for the symmetric-six source

For three distinct supported projective roots r,s,h, take linear forms
 alpha=(s-h)(t-r), beta=(h-r)(t-s), gamma=(r-s)(t-h).
They sum to zero. For h=infinity use alpha=-(t-r), beta=t-s, gamma=s-r.
For parameter q, put
 W=alpha+beta*q^2,
 U=W-2(alpha+beta*q), V=W-2q(alpha+beta*q).
Then alpha*U^2+beta*V^2+gamma*W^2=0, and
 f=-alpha*U^2/(gamma*W^2)
has the required two-anchor norm classes. There are 35 triples times six
anchor transformations, hence 210 families. All rational parameter exceptions
and infinity are checked as before.

### New Lean theorem: a degree-independent support-pattern obstruction

Submission/HeptadResidualSquareClasses.lean is complete and has an installed
olean. It imports only FormalConjecturesUtil. All four printed axiom audits
use only propext,Classical.choice,Quot.sound. The build is warning-free, exit 0:

rootEval evaluates the six homogeneous root factors at the six projective
roots (with a harmless choice of sign for infinity). The kernel-decided
branch_square_obstruction says that for five DISTINCT supported roots
r,s,a,b,c, the two rational classes
 rootEval(s,a)/rootEval(r,a) * rootEval(r,b)/rootEval(s,b),
 rootEval(s,a)/rootEval(r,a) * rootEval(r,c)/rootEval(s,c)
cannot BOTH be squares. This is the full ordered finite certificate, not an
import of the external 60-case result.

compatible_values_force_square is a general rational algebra lemma. From
 alpha*A0*u0^2=beta*B0*v0^2 and
 alpha*A1*u1^2=beta*B1*v1^2,
with the specified nonzero denominators and beta!=0, it proves
 IsSquare(B0/A0*A1/B1), with witness v1*u0/(u1*v0).
The proof is by a polynomial identity and legitimate field cancellation.

no_three_compatible_values combines these results. Two simple-supported
square forms at roots r,s cannot agree nontrivially at three other supported
roots a,b,c. The values U,V at those roots are ARBITRARY nonzero rationals;
no polynomial degree or coefficient-height bound is assumed. Thus this
rigorously excludes the one-squarefree-supported-cubic/two-square-residual
pattern, and the same evaluation obstruction applies to higher-degree square
factors with that support pattern. It does not exclude other support patterns
or arbitrary rational-distance configurations.

### Degree-three normal-form reasoning for the heptad (not kernel formalized)

For generic t and conjugate(t), the two anchor norms force each of the three
coprime polynomials A,B,B-A separately to be a square times supported factors.
At homogeneous degree <=3, a cubic is either fully supported or has exactly
one supported simple root times a squared linear form. Repeated supported
roots already fall in the latter case. Degree-two polynomials are supported
or squared linear forms. Constants and infinity factors are included.

If two cubics are fully supported, the finite catalog covers them. If just
one is fully supported and has three distinct projective roots, the new Lean
square-class obstruction excludes the other two simple-supported-square forms.
For three simple-supported-square forms, evaluating at their three distinct
supported simple roots fixes their scalar coefficient square classes. After
rational rescaling the identity is
 alpha*U^2+beta*V^2+gamma*W^2=0,
with alpha+beta+gamma=0 and U,V,W homogeneous linear forms.

A useful completeness argument for the displayed conic parametrization is:
if the coefficient matrix of U,V,W has rank two, its image is a projective
line. The two diagonal quadrics obtained as coefficients of t in the conic
identity restrict to binary quadrics with a common linear factor (their
linear-in-t identity forces this). Their common base points are the four
sign variants of (1,1,1). Thus the image line goes through one of these base
points. Changing signs of U,V,W does not change the represented squares, and
reduces to the constant-slope line through (1,1,1) used by the producer. The
slope at infinity is included. Rank-one images give the degree-one limiting
functions. This explains why rational-function parameters of positive degree
in that conic parametrization do not give additional primitive cubics.

Together with the analogous quadratic S/S/L reduction, these arguments
support coverage of nonconstant generic degree<=3 extensions of this fixed
heptad. The normal-form wrapper and external finite lists have NOT been
formalized as a full Lean classification theorem. In particular this is not
an unrestricted GP8 nonexistence theorem: higher degree, functions involving
the input square roots, and arithmetic specializations remain unexcluded.

## Literal Pythagorean quartic extensions of the heptad (MAIN NOT SOLVED)

This continuation tests a new quartic construction class, not a larger
coefficient-height window. It does not settle the main conjecture.

### Specified class and necessary finite root systems

Use the normalized heptad
 [0,1,-t/2,t(t+1)/2,(t+1)/2,t^2,(t+1)^2]
and the five finite supported roots {-2,-1,-1/2,0,1}.
The class under study is
 f=phi^2, degree(phi)<=2, and 1-phi^2 is a square in Q(t).
Both are LITERAL rational-function squares, not merely rational constants
times squares. A nonconstant phi is bounded in [-1,1] on the real line and
has no real poles. Its reduced denominator B must have degree two (a
nonconstant real rational function of degree at most one cannot be bounded),
with strictly negative discriminant. Normalize B=t^2+b1*t+b0 and write
A=a2*t^2+a1*t+a0, phi=A/B.

If the generic norms to t^2 and (t+1)^2 pass, the polynomial numerators
 A-tB, A+tB, A-(t+1)B, A+(t+1)B
have only supported odd factors. Indeed each pair's product has that
property, and the pair's gcd is supported at t=0 or t=-1 since A,B are
coprime. Each numerator is cubic, hence has an allowed finite real root.
Boundedness of phi restricts the first two roots to {-1,-1/2,0,1} and the
last two to {-2,-1,-1/2,0}: 256 root assignments, not a parameter-height
search. At a root where phi is +/-1, A-phi(root)*B has a double zero, so its
derivative supplies an additional linear coefficient equation.

The two necessary quadratic equations are disc(B-A)=disc(B+A)=0. They
follow from 1-phi^2 being a square and coprimality; a nonconstant linear
factor cannot occur to odd multiplicity. Constant and degree-drop cases
are retained by these equations.

### Completion of all three retained cases

Rows 51 and 204 have A=-B and A=B identically, so f=1 is already present.
Row 165 has
 A=a*t*(t+1), B=t^2+b*t+c,
with necessary equations
 a^2+b^2=4c, a*(2c-b)=0.
The a=0 branch is constant/degenerate. Otherwise b=2c and
 a^2=4c(1-c). Negative denominator discriminant gives 0<c<1. Put
 k=a/(2c), so k!=0,
 c=1/(1+k^2), a=2k/(1+k^2).
Thus
 phi=2k*t*(t+1)/(k^2*t^2+(t+1)^2).

Write Bk=k^2*t^2+(t+1)^2 and
 Qplus=Bk+2k(t+1), Qminus=Bk-2k(t+1).
The exact identity is
 (2k*t*(t+1))^2-t^2*Bk^2=-t^2*Qplus*Qminus.
Their discriminants are -8k^3 and 8k^3. For EVERY real k!=0 one quadratic is
irreducible over R, so it has no supported real root. It appears to odd
multiplicity. The correct resultants (including the leading-coefficient
factor) are
 Res(Bk,Qplus)=Res(Bk,Qminus)=4k^4(k^2+1),
 Res(Qplus,Qminus)=16k^4(k^2+1).
They are nonzero for real k!=0, so neither cancellation nor a special
nonzero parameter repairs the generic norm. The independent audit verifies
all these identities. The omitted (k^2+1) factor in an initial handwritten
resultant guess was caught and corrected before the passing audit.

### New kernel-checked obstruction for the retained family

Submission/PythagoreanQuarticObstruction.lean is COMPLETE, with installed
olean, no holes/warnings, and four permitted-axiom audits. Final build:
 /tmp/pythagorean_quartic_obstruction_lean.{log,exit}, exit 0.
It imports only FormalConjecturesUtil.

It defines Bk, Qplus=quad(k), Qminus=quad(-k), and
 numerator(k)=X^2*quad(k)*quad(-k).
`numerator_identity` verifies the displayed polynomial factorization.
For k>0, `quad_positive` proves quad(k)(x)>0 for every real x from
 4(k^2+1)quad(k)(x)=(2(k^2+1)x+2(1+k))^2+8k^3.
The polynomial has degree two and is irreducible over R. Exact divisibility
lemmas show it divides neither X nor quad(-k), using their difference
C(4k)*(X+1), not an external resultant certificate.

The general lemma `not_split_times_square` proves that an irreducible
polynomial with no real root cannot occur to odd order in S*H^2 with S split
over R. Prime divisibility forces it into H, after which cancellation forces

`heptad_quartic_finite_residuals.sage` examines primitive homogeneous quartic

For 222, evaluating at the six supported roots determines the three rational

### One-parameter 004 and 002 pencils

`heptad_quartic_pencil_extensions.sage` uses the full polynomial norm, including
the denominator, and enumerates all rational exceptional parameters through
content, leading coefficient, discriminant, and supported-root evaluations.
Infinity is checked separately. There is no parameter-height bound.

004 consists of

  f=(P+q*Q)^2/(4*q*P*Q),

where P,Q are disjoint supported quadratics. The 45 partitions and six anchor
transforms give 270 one-parameter families.

002 has the form

  f=(P+lambda*W^2)^2/(4*lambda*P*W^2),

with P supported quadratic and W linear. The following necessary-root argument
reduces its two parameters to finitely many one-parameter curves:

* If P has two finite roots and W=t-u, the numerator of f+t/2 has degree five.
  At a supported finite root r, put z=lambda*W(r)^2/P(r). The equation
  (z+1)^2=-2*r*z permits only r=-2 or r=0. Thus lambda is respectively
  P(-2)/(-2-u)^2 or -P(0)/u^2. A root of P cannot be used in a primitive pencil.
* If P includes infinity, the numerator of f-t^2 has degree five. Its supported
  rational roots can only be -1,0,1. A zero at 0 has multiplicity exactly two:
  f vanishes there to even order with negative leading sign, so f-t^2 has a
  nonzero negative quadratic term. Thus an odd root must be -1 or 1, giving
  lambda=P(r)/(r-u)^2.
* The chart W=1 is separately included with unrestricted rational lambda.
* Common factors of P,W reduce the function degree and are not primitive
  degree-four cases. The lower-degree catalogs were already completed.

These give 210 further one-parameter families. Across all 480 families there
are 500 distinct specialized functions: 497 fail further norms and three are
existing source points. No uniform compatible family or new point occurs.

## Constant-square quartic charts and arithmetic defect profiles (MAIN NOT SOLVED)

This is still restricted-function analysis, not an unrestricted GP bound.
The primitive homogeneous degree-four squarefree-support counts can only be
000,002,004,022,024,222, up to permutation. The following coverage arguments
for 000 remain mathematical normal-form arguments, not a complete Lean
classification of rational functions or rational-distance point sets.

### Negative constant-square chart

For f=a*phi^2 and 1-f=b*psi^2 with nonzero rational a,b, a finite-at-infinity
quartic has a degree-five numerator for f+t/2. It therefore needs an odd
supported finite root. In the negative range f<=0, that root is either 0
(forcing b square) or 1 (forcing a,b to have classes -2,6). In the range f>=1,
the root must be -2 (forcing a square). These statements concern the real
rational-function values at rational supported roots, not complex evaluations.

The branch-at-zero pencil is

  f=4*A*t^2*(t-u)^2 / ((t-u)^2+A*t^2)^2,

with A,u nonzero. If 0 is its only odd supported root for f+t/2, the residual
quartic ((t-u)^2+A*t^2)^2+8*A*t*(t-u)^2 must be a polynomial square. Its
coefficient equations are inconsistent. The chart with constant linear
factor is separately excluded. The branch-at-one case, after shifting the
root -2 to 0, reduces by t -> -t to the same obstruction.

For the remaining classes (-2,6), use x=t-1, W=x+h, K=k*x and

  U=K^2-4*K*W-2*W^2,
  B=K^2+2*K*W-2*W^2,
  V=-(K^2+2*W^2),
  f=-U^2/(2*B^2).

The identity -2*U^2+6*V^2=4*B^2 holds. The residual polynomial
((x+1)*B^2-U^2)/x must be a square. Its leading coefficient is
(k^2+2*k-2)^2, nonzero for rational k. Matching the next two coefficients
fixes the proposed quadratic square root and leaves two polynomial equations
in k,h. An independent resultant, after removing only forbidden monomial
factors, is a nonzero rational constant times

  h^20*(h-3)^2*(h-1)^2*(2*h-3).

The rational coefficient solutions are

  (h,k)=(0,2),(0,-1),(3,0),(1,0),(3/2,-2).

Only the last is a nonconstant primitive parameter pair. Its function passes
the norms to 0,1,-t/2, but fails EACH of the other four source norms. The
separate constant-denominator chart gives the unit ideal. No GP8 is obtained.

Sources:

  heptad_quartic_negative_twist.sage
  check_heptad_quartic_negative_twist.sage
  audit_heptad_quartic_negative.py

The independent audit uses resultants and rational roots, not Sage's variety

It also checks the critical-branch coefficient ideals; the correct eliminated

### Positive and infinite-value 000 charts: scope of the reductions

If a,b>0 and a is a rational square, f=phi^2 is bounded in [0,1]. The earlier
256 root systems apply even if 1-f is a positive nonsquare constant times a
square: the necessary discriminant equations for B+U and B-U are unchanged.
The four finite nonliteral occurrences were already separately checked
(they have 1-f in class 3, represented there as 27 times a square) and fail
further norms. The retained curves were excluded independently of that
literal-square assumption by PythagoreanQuarticObstruction.

If a,b>0 and a is nonsquare, f-t^2 and f-(t+1)^2 have no odd rational roots.
A nonzero rational root would force a square; at the zero square-anchor root,
positivity gives multiplicity exactly two. Thus their generic norm conditions
force negative literal squares. Evaluating at 0 and -1 makes the quadratic
numerator of phi a constant multiple of t(t+1). The denominator would then
make both B^2-A*t^2 and B^2-A*(t+1)^2 polynomial squares for A!=0. The new
all-degree polynomial theorem below rules this out for degree(B)>=2.

If the denominator of a primitive 000 quartic has affine degree one, its
infinite pole forces opposite coefficient square classes. The conic chart is
f=(A*(t-u)^2+1)^2/(4*A*(t-u)^2). The only possible odd supported roots of
f+t/2 are 0 and -2, but both cannot occur since they would force opposite
signs of A. Its residual numerator must therefore be a literal square.
After centering at u, that polynomial is

  (A*X^2+1)^2+2*A*(X+u)*X^2,

which is excluded by the new kernel theorem. A constant denominator would
make a polynomial difference of two squares constant, forcing a constant map.

These reductions support the stated quartic exclusions. They have NOT been
assembled into a Lean normal-form/classification theorem. They do not apply
to arbitrary-degree functions or isolated arithmetic square values.

## One structured quintic chart: exact square classification (MAIN NOT SOLVED)

This continuation carried out the single proposed degree-five test. It is
NOT a classification of all quintics, all rational functions, or arbitrary
rational-distance configurations. No arithmetic specialization search was
performed, and no new point or unbounded construction was obtained.

### Chart and first extra norm

With N=t+a, D=t+c, set

  W=-t*D^2+(t+1)*N^2,
  L=-t*D+(t+1)*N,
  U=W-2*L*D,
  V=W-2*L*N.

All three forms U,V,W are quadratic, and

  -t*U^2+(t+1)*V^2-W^2=0.

For f=-t*U^2/W^2, the norm classes to 0 and 1 are automatic.
The additional difference to -t/2 is t*(W^2-2U^2)/(2W^2).
If U,W are coprime, W^2-2U^2 has no rational root: such a root
would either give a common root or make 2 a rational square.
Thus its generic supported-factor condition forces it to be a
constant times a polynomial square. Evaluation at t=-1, where
U(-1)=-(c-1)^2 and W(-1)=(c-1)^2, fixes the square class.
Consequently the required literal identity is

  2*U^2-W^2=H^2.

This is a generic function-field implication, NOT an implication from
an accidental square at an individual quadratic arithmetic parameter.
The connection to the generic norm predicate is described mathematically
here; the new Lean module verifies the polynomial classification itself.

The exact resultant is

  resultant_t(U,W)=4*a*(a-c)^4*(c-1)^2.

All common-factor boundaries are tracked:

* a=c: U=-(t+c)^2, W=(t+c)^2 and f=-t.
* c=1: U=(t+1)*(-t+a*(a-2)),
       W=(t+1)*((2*a-1)*t+a^2); the reduced degree is at most three.
* a=0: U=-t*(t-c^2+2*c), W=-t*((2*c-1)*t+c^2);
       again the reduced degree is at most three.

The square classification below assumes only a!=c and c!=1, so it also
rules out a=0 under those other hypotheses. A drop in the leading
coefficient of W does not need exclusion: U always has leading coefficient -1.

### Exact coefficient elimination

Write x=t+1. A proposed square root has constant coefficient
+(c-1)^2 after changing its sign if needed. Its next two coefficients are

  B=-3*a^2+4*a*c+2*a-c^2-2,
  D=(-4*a^4+8*a^3*c+8*a^3-4*a^2*c^2-16*a^2*c-4*a^2
     +6*a*c^2+12*a*c-2*a+2*c^3-7*c^2+1)/(c-1)^2.

Let

  F=-3*a^2+a*c+5*a+c-4,
  G=-2*a^5+2*a^4*c+8*a^4-8*a^3*c-12*a^3-2*a^2*c^2
     +16*a^2*c+6*a^2+5*a*c^2-18*a*c+3*a+c^3-6*c^2+11*c-4.

The remaining cubic and quartic coefficient discrepancies are exactly

  8*(a-c)^3*(a-1)*F/(c-1)^2,
  8*(a-c)^3*G/(c-1)^4.

Away from a=c,c=1, a=1 is impossible since G(1,c)=(c-1)^3.
The independent audit and Lean proof use the explicit elimination identity

  (a+1)^3*G-F*Q=2*(a-2)^2*(a-1)^5*(2*a-1),

where

  Q=2*a^6-10*a^5-2*a^4*c+30*a^4+4*a^3*c-50*a^3
    +a^2*c^2+39*a^2+2*a*c^2-8*a*c-10*a+c^2-2*c+3.

The branch a=2 forces c=2 and is excluded. Therefore the unique solution
on the specified chart is

  (a,c)=(1/2,3/2).

It really is a square: in x coordinates the square root is x^2+x-1/4.
Sage's independent Groebner computation gives the same solution; the
audit and Lean argument do not rely on that Groebner solver.

### The surviving candidate fails the other four generic norms

The candidate is

  f=-t*(4*t^2+8*t+5)^2/(4*t^2+4*t-1)^2.

Its first three differences have supported square classes. Each of the
remaining four differences has an unsupported odd factor, respectively

  16*t^5+80*t^4+168*t^3+208*t^2+153*t+51,
  48*t^5+176*t^4+248*t^3+160*t^2+43*t+1,
  16*t^4+32*t^3+40*t^2+56*t+25,
  16*t^6+80*t^5+152*t^4+144*t^3+73*t^2+19*t+1.

The independent audit checks that all four are squarefree and nonzero at
all five supported finite roots. In particular, the third polynomial P
satisfies P(0)=25 and P(-1)=-7, so it cannot be any rational constant times
a polynomial square, regardless of the proposed square root's degree.
This latter obstruction is also proved in Lean. No isolated arithmetic
nonexistence conclusion follows from these generic failures.

## Product-octad norm matching and Cayley change (MAIN NOT SOLVED)

This continuation works on the product template {±1,±b,±c,±bc}, without a
fixed source-height search. It obtains two complete restricted Lean modules,
not a GP8, a growing construction, or an unrestricted upper bound.

### One proportional matching forces square characteristic

Put b=x+y*sqrt(-D), c=z+w*sqrt(-D), with rational coordinates, and

 r=x^2+D*y^2, s=z^2+D*w^2,
 M_b=(x-1)^2+D*y^2, P_b=(x+1)^2+D*y^2,
 M_c=(z-1)^2+D*w^2, P_c=(z+1)^2+D*w^2.

A sufficient way to make the two missing norms rational would be to have
one rational proportionality factor L satisfying

 |bc-1|^2=L^2*|b-c|^2,
 |bc+1|^2=L^2*|b+c|^2.

This SAME-SIGN matching, not a crossed matching or an arbitrary extension,
is now restricted uniformly. The proof even allows an arbitrary rational
q in place of L^2. Adding and subtracting the equations gives

 rs+1=q*(r+s),
 xz-Dyw=q*(xz+Dyw).

Eliminating q yields

 (r-1)(s-1)*xz+D*(r+1)(s+1)*yw=0.

Define the two rational coordinate vectors

 J_b=(x*(r-1), y*(r+1)),
 J_c=(z*(s-1), w*(s+1)).

They are the numerator vectors for b-1/b and c-1/c. Their squared norms are

 N(J_b)=r*M_b*P_b, N(J_c)=s*M_c*P_c,

and their D-inner product is zero. If r,M_b,P_b,s,M_c,P_c are nonzero rational
squares, both J vectors have nonzero rational lengths. The Gram identity

 (a^2+D*b^2)(c^2+D*d^2)=(ac+Dbd)^2+D(ad-bc)^2

then makes D a rational square. The proof supplies the square root explicitly
as the product of the two rational lengths divided by ad-bc, whose nonzero
value follows from the same identity. No classification of elliptic points,
height restriction, or numerical premise is used.

NEW `Submission/ProductNormMatching.lean` is complete, warning-free, with
installed olean and SEVEN permitted-axiom audits. It proves the norm identity,
the general perpendicular-vector theorem, the matching restriction, the
radius equation and elliptic necessary equation, the direct Cartesian norm
bridges, and a nontrivial radius-only positive control.

This does NOT show that all product octads have square characteristic:
the extra proportional matching is a substantive hypothesis. The crossed
matching is not covered. Even with this matching, the square-characteristic
case remains unrestricted by this theorem.

### The radius-only equation is not itself an obstruction

Writing r=R^2, s=S^2, q=L^2 gives

 (R^2+S^2)*L^2=R^2*S^2+1.

It maps to

 E_R: Y^2=X(X+1)(X+R^4),
 X=R^2*S^2, Y=R^2*S*(R^2+S^2)*L.

This necessary equation has the nondegenerate rational control

 R=5/2, S=24/11, L=122/73.

Both the equality and nonvanishing of
R*S*(R^2-1)*(S^2-1)*(R^2-S^2) are kernel verified. These three numbers do
NOT specify b,c, anchor distances, or a rational-distance point set.

The preliminary exact Sage diagnostic reported ranks 0,0,0,0,1 for E_R at
R=2,3,4,3/2,5/2, respectively, each with torsion invariants (2,4). These are
external diagnostics only; the Lean results use none of the rank assertions.
For R=5/2 the point (-125/4,1375/16) doubles to
(3600/121,-333975/1331), yielding S=24/11 and L=-122/73.
The independent audit checks that doubling by direct Fraction arithmetic.

An initial radius-control script omitted one factor R in the denominator
of L. Its failed assertion was corrected to the displayed formula with R^2;
the final successful control and Lean theorem use the corrected identity.

### A norm-preserving Cayley change, periodic up to similarity

For F(z)=(z-1)/(z+1), the exact identities are

 F(b)-F(c)=2(b-c)/((b+1)(c+1)),
 F(b)+F(c)=2(bc-1)/((b+1)(c+1)),
 F(b)F(c)-1=-2(b+c)/((b+1)(c+1)),
 F(b)F(c)+1=2(bc+1)/((b+1)(c+1)).

Together with F(b)-1=-2/(b+1) and F(b)+1=2b/(b+1), they show that the ten
rational norm inputs b,c,b±1,c±1,b±c,bc±1 survive the simultaneous Cayley
change, away from b=-1 or c=-1. This does not supply the input conditions.

NEW `Submission/ProductCayley.lean` is complete, warning-free, with installed
olean and FOUR permitted-axiom audits. It formalizes the identities and norm
preservation using the earlier RationalNorm/Compatible predicates.
It also proves F(F(b))=-1/b when the needed denominators are nonzero. For

 P(b,c)=[1,-1,b,-b,c,-c,bc,-bc],
 pi=[6,7,5,4,3,2,0,1],

it proves, for EVERY index i,

 P(F(F(b)),F(F(c)))[i]=P(b,c)[pi(i)]/(bc).

The corresponding actual complex Euclidean distance scaling is verified.
Thus two applications give a relabelled similarity, not a repeatable source
of new shapes. No universal GP-preservation or GP-obstruction statement is
claimed for the FIRST application.

  1+S^2, R^2+S^2, 1+R^2*S^2.

  (X^2-S^4)^2+4*S^4*Y^2=(X^2+2*S^4*X+S^4)^2

supply the latter two square conditions. The first is a separate hypothesis.

## Product matching orientation fiber and four-square cover (MAIN NOT SOLVED)

This continuation tests whether the product matching can give a genuine
metric growth rule, rather than enlarging a finite coordinate catalog.
It obtains a new exact orientation reduction and two complete auxiliary Lean
modules. It does NOT obtain an eight-point rational-distance configuration,
an arbitrary-cardinality construction, or an unrestricted upper bound.

### Matching alone is not a geometric degeneracy condition

The same-sign matching equation from ProductNormMatching is, in D=1,

  M=(r-1)(s-1)*xz+(r+1)(s+1)*yw=0,
  r=x^2+y^2, s=z^2+w^2.

product_matching_geometry.sage compared M and the corresponding crossed
polynomial against all 70 four-point circle determinants of
{1,-1,b,-b,c,-c,bc,-bc}. No common polynomial factor was found. This external
symbolic test is not a nonexistence theorem and does not supply rational
metric inputs. Its relevance is superseded by the exact geometric control
below, which actually satisfies matching and general position while failing
the rational-distance requirements.

Artifact /tmp/product_matching_geometry.{json,log,exit}, exit 0.

### An elliptic orientation fiber above the radius-only control

Fix the earlier necessary-equation control

  R=5/2, S=24/11, L=122/73,
  (R^2+S^2)*L^2=R^2*S^2+1.

Set r=R^2, s=S^2 and

  k=(r+1)(s+1)/((r-1)(s-1))=20213/9555,
  H=2L(r+s)/((r-1)(s-1))=17812/9555,
  k^2-H^2=1.

For A=9555, B=20213 and rational e,u,v satisfying

  u^2=e^2+A^2, v^2=e^2+B^2, u*v!=0,

put

  b=(R*e/u, R*A/u), c=(S*B/v, -S*e/v).

Both radii are correct, and the same-sign matching with factor L^2 holds.
These facts do NOT make the six further norms b±1,c±1,b±c rational.
The two-square fiber is parametrized by doubled points on

  E: Y^2=X(X+A^2)(X+B^2).

For an input point (X,Y), Y!=0, the exact formulas are

  e=(X^2-A^2*B^2)/(2Y),
  u=(X^2+2A^2*X+A^2*B^2)/(2Y),
  v=(X^2+2B^2*X+A^2*B^2)/(2Y).

Sage reported rank 1 and torsion (2,4), with point

  (25593225,1139666309250).

The formulas give

  e=-80388/5, u=93513/5, v=129137/5,
  b=(-9570/4453,11375/8906),
  c=(83640/48983,6048/4453).

All eight product points are distinct. All 56 triangle determinants and all
70 circle determinants are nonzero. However ONLY FOUR of their 28 distances
are rational. All six missing square norms fail:

  205697/17812, 52577/17812,
  1263661/538813, 4943821/538813,
  26798809/1800964, 12859609/1800964.

Thus this is an eight-point GEOMETRIC control with irrational edges, not a
rational-distance GP8. It refutes any claim that matching and rational radii
alone either force geometric degeneracy or ensure the remaining metric edges.

### The missing requirements force a four-square cover

For this fixed fiber let C=13195 and D=14637. The exact identities are

  u^2*N(b-1)*N(b+1)=(21/4)^2*(e^2+C^2),
  v^2*N(c-1)*N(c+1)=(697/121)^2*(e^2+C^2),
  u^2*v^2*N(b-c)*N(b+c)=(5329/484)^2*(e^2+C^2)*(e^2+D^2).

Here N is squared Euclidean norm. Consequently the b±1 and b±c square
requirements, together with the two orientation equations, force ALL FOUR
of

  e^2+9555^2, e^2+20213^2, e^2+13195^2, e^2+14637^2

to be rational squares. This is a necessary condition, NOT a converse. In
particular e=0 satisfies all four squares but the b-anchor norm for u=9555
is 29/4, not a rational square. The nonzero displayed orientation control
fails both newly required squares.

An independently checked general algebraic factorization behind the third
identity is

  (t^2+a^2)(t^2+a^2*f^2*g^2)
    -t^2*a^2*(f^2-1)*(g^2-1)
  =(t^2+a^2*f^2)(t^2+a^2*g^2).

For general non-unit radii the analogous scales are A, A*f*g, A*f, A*g,
with f=(r+1)/(r-1), g=(s+1)/(s-1). The new Lean four-cover theorem is for
the displayed FIXED fiber; it is not stated as a universal arithmetic
classification or as a theorem about arbitrary integral point sets.
Infinitely many points on the orientation elliptic curve do not establish
infinitely many rational points on this extra square cover.

## Entire fixed-radius matching family excluded modulo 19 (MAIN NOT SOLVED)

This continuation proves an arithmetic obstruction for ALL rational points in
the latest radius/matching family, rather than testing more elliptic points.
It does not settle Erdős 213.

### Exact local obstruction

For the radius-only control R=5/2, S=24/11, L=122/73, the initial finite-field
diagnostic considered primes 3 mod 4, excluding 2,11,73. It stopped at the
first obstruction, 19. It did NOT test every prime up to its loop limit.
No general-position condition was imposed on residue points.

 p=3: b-anchor options 2, c-anchor options 1; matching/metric pairs 2;
 p=7: b-anchor options 4, c-anchor options 4; matching/metric pairs 12;
 p=19: b-anchor options 2, c-anchor options 6; matching pairs 0.

At p=19 the radii reduce to 12 and 16, and L to 10. The first radius and
both b-anchor square conditions force y=0. Matching then forces z=0, but
c's radius and anchor conditions would require 10 to be a nonzero square
modulo 19, which it is not.

The final theorem does NOT assume that rational coordinates have denominators
prime to 19. That gap is resolved by homogenization and infinite descent.

### Homogeneous system and kernel proof

New complete file Submission/ProductOrientationLocal.lean (295 lines).
Coordinates are j=(t,x,y,z,w,a,b,c,d), and the seven homogeneous equations are

  4*(x^2+y^2)-25*t^2=0,
  121*(z^2+w^2)-576*t^2=0,
  a^2-(x-t)^2-y^2=0,
  b^2-(x+t)^2-y^2=0,
  c^2-(z-t)^2-w^2=0,
  d^2-(z+t)^2-w^2=0,
  9555*x*z+20213*y*w=0.

The last equation follows from the earlier same-sign matching orthogonality
identity after substituting the two squared radii and multiplying by 484.
In particular the proportionality factor q may be ANY rational number; the
proof does not need q=L^2.

Kernel-checked finite-field lemmas prove:

 * x^2+y^2=0 over F_19 implies x=y=0;
 * the homogeneous first-radius and two anchor-square conditions imply y=0;
 * 121*w^2=576*t^2 and IsSquare(t^2+w^2) imply t=0.

They imply that every homogeneous solution over F_19 is the zero vector.
The t=0 hyperplane is included: anisotropy forces x=y=z=w=0, and then all
four anchor-root coordinates vanish as well. Thus no point at infinity is
silently discarded.

For an integral solution, all nine coordinates are divisible by 19. All
seven equations are homogeneous of degree two, so division by 19 preserves
them. Strong induction on a coordinate's absolute value proves that every
integral solution is zero. Clearing denominators with
IsLocalization.exist_integer_multiples_of_finite then proves the same for
rational solutions. The intended affine input has t=1 and is impossible.

The resulting theorem is

  fixed_radii_no_matching:
    radius 1 x y=(5/2)^2 -> radius 1 z w=(24/11)^2 ->
    SquareInput 1 x y -> SquareInput 1 z w ->
    Matching 1 x y z w q -> False.

 N(bc-1)=u^2-3v-u+1,

therefore gives (3u+1)v=(u-1)(u^2+1). If r=R^2, s=S^2,

 X=10*(u-1)/(3u+1), Y=40*P/(3u+1)

## Crossed zero-sum quotient: complete elementary descent (MAIN NOT SOLVED)

This continuation closes the previously missing rational-point classification
for the crossed zero-sum quotient. It does not settle the original conjecture.

### Kernel-verified reduction

New complete `Submission/ProductCrossZeroSum.lean` proves the earlier audited
norm identities for b=x+y*sqrt(-D), c=-1-b. With u=N(b)+N(c), v=N(b)N(c),
the CROSSED equations

 N(bc-1)=q*N(b+c), N(bc+1)=q*N(b-c)

imply

 (3u+1)v=(u-1)(u^2+1),
 (3u+1)q=u^2-u+4.

If D>0 and y!=0, both radii are positive and u>1. If both radii are rational
squares, v=P^2, and the explicitly verified map

 X=10*(u-1)/(3u+1), Y=40*P/(3u+1)

produces a rational point with X!=0 on Y^2=X^3-4X^2+20X. The algebra file
alone makes no claim about rational points on this curve. Its positive
matching control D=1,x=0,y=1,q=1 has radii 1 and 2, so is NOT a rational-
distance source. The file compiled warning-free and prints seven permitted-
axiom audits; its olean is installed.

### Elementary quartic descent, not a Sage rank premise

New complete `Submission/CrossQuarticDescent.lean` proves that

 w^2=t^4-4t^2+20

has no rational solution. The primitive integral form is

 c^2+4a^2b^2=a^4+20b^4, gcd(a,b)=1, b>0.

The descent works as follows.

1. Modulo 32, primitivity forces a and c odd. Also gcd(c,b)=1.
2. Set d=|a^2-2b^2|. Then c^2=d^2+16b^4, d is odd and gcd(c,d)=1.
   Coprime half-sum/half-difference factors have product 4b^4. Consequently
   b=mn, gcd(m,n)=1, c=m^4+4n^4, and m is odd.
3. The quartic gives

     (a^2-2m^2n^2)^2=(m^4-4n^4)^2.

   The negative branch is impossible modulo 16. The positive branch is

     a^2+4n^4=m^4+2m^2n^2,

   and modulo 16 it forces n even.
4. Rewrite this as a^2+5n^4=(m^2+n^2)^2. The two quantities a and m^2+n^2
   are coprime. For the potentially exceptional prime 5, divisibility of
   both would force 5|n and then 5|m, contradicting gcd(m,n)=1; this is
   proved with exact divisibility, not assumed from a local diagnostic.
5. Write n=2N. The coprime half-sum/half-difference factors now have product
   20N^4. Thus N=rs, gcd(r,s)=1, and their sum is either

     20r^4+s^4 or 4r^4+5s^4.

   The second case is impossible modulo 16 since m is odd. The first gives

     m^2+4s^2r^2=s^4+20r^4,

   a new primitive solution with denominator r. Since n=2rs and b=mn with
   m,r,s>0, r<b. Strong induction on b proves impossibility.
6. Clearing the rational denominator with `Rat.isSquare_intCast_iff` produces
   exactly such a primitive integral solution, including all possible signs
   of t and w by natural absolute values.

The proof reuses only complete arithmetic helpers from OrthogonalGlobal;
no Mordell-Weil theorem, external rank assertion, or finite-height search is
used. In particular it does not make the invalid jump from local 2-descent
images to a rank conclusion.

### Duplication gives the full elliptic classification

For any rational point (x,y) on y^2=x^3-4x^2+20x with y!=0, the exact
polynomial identity underlying duplication gives a quartic solution

 t=(x^2-20)/(2y),
 w=(x^4-8x^3+120x^2-160x+400)/(4y^2).

The quartic impossibility therefore forces y=0. Positivity of
x^2-4x+20=(x-2)^2+16 then forces x=0. This proves

 elliptic_points : y^2=x^3-4x^2+20x -> x=0 and y=0.

It further proves

 quotient_classification:
   (3u+1)P^2=(u-1)(u^2+1) -> u=1 and P=0.

The denominator exceptional case 3u+1=0 is explicitly excluded from the
original polynomial equation, not silently discarded.

Finally `zero_sum_matching_degenerate` proves that, for D>0 and both radii
rational squares, EVERY crossed zero-sum matching has

 y=0 and (x=0 or x=-1).

Thus one of b,c is zero. `no_crossed_zero_sum` excludes the nonreal case.
This is stronger than only testing the classical central source at finitely
many parameter values. It is still restricted to the zero-sum and crossed-
matching assumptions, neither of which follows from an arbitrary point set.

modulo 3 or 5. Every certificate multiplier is nonzero by output injectivity
or by the assumption that reflection does not fix the singleton. The 16
nonfixing factors used across the certificates concern the singleton itself,
not a stronger assumption that the reflection differs from every old point.

`no_reflection_case` proves: if t satisfies a monic rational quadratic,
the seven outputs are distinct, and the three pair sums equal C, then
C-Psingleton cannot differ from Psingleton. No general-position assumption
is needed for this fixed-singleton conclusion.

`CentralReflectionPairing.lean` removes any restriction on labelling. Its
5040 permutation witnesses are split into 84 literal blocks of 60 entries.
Each entry carries its matching index; the kernel checks the singleton and
unordered pairs. A separate kernel equality verifies that projecting the
certificate list gives exactly `(List.finRange 7).permutations'`. Thus no
external completeness premise or native-decide axiom is used. The general
permutation wrapper, fixed-singleton theorem, and no-paired-six theorem all
pass permitted-axiom audits.

The wrapper initially uses only rational norms of t and 1-t to obtain a
quadratic equation. A centrally paired six-point subset would put the seventh
at its center, producing a collinear triple. Hence a NonTrilinear output has
no such subset. `CentralReflectionGeneral.lean` removes normalization using

    point a b c i = a^2 * points (b/a) (c/a) i.

Injectivity forces a nonzero. Only the three source norms of a, b, and a-b
are used in this wrapper, not all nine usual construction hypotheses.

### Explicit metric inverse (Lean verified)

`CentralMetricInverse.lean` supplies a stronger, output-only bridge. Set
Dij=L*(Pi-Pj), where L is any nonzero complex scale. For distinct outputs,
all displayed denominators are nonzero, and Lean verifies

    t   = D35*D21/(D32*D45),
    w   = D34*D21/(D31*D45),
    1+t = 2*D31/D36,       1-t = 2*D16/D36,
    1+w = 2*D32/D36,       1-w = 2*D26/D36,
    t+w = 2*D21/D45,       t-w = 2*D21/D36,
    L   = D36/(2*(t+w)).

Together with the trivial factor 1 these recover all nine normalized source
norms from output distances. `scaled_output_distances_iff` proves an exact
equivalence: all scaled output distances are rational iff L has rational norm
and all nine normalized source factors have rational norms. The converse uses
the earlier 21 difference factorizations. In particular accidental rational
outputs from irrational normalized source norms, even after a common complex
scale, cannot bypass the source conditions.

`CentralOutputField.lean` gives an independent quadratic-field bridge using
rational Gram entries. The output sums recover 4L and 4Lt, so rational output
distances imply that t satisfies a rational quadratic. This bridge does not
assume rational source norms.

`CentralOutputReflection.lean` combines the metric inverse with the complete
matching obstruction. Rationality is assumed only for the seven scaled
outputs. Any centrally paired six outputs force the seventh to be their
center; a NonTrilinear output therefore has no centrally paired six-point
subset. This rules out this affine reflection extension of the central
quadratic heptad, not all seven-to-eight extensions or all point sets.

## Cyclic-cubic resolvent metric probe (MAIN NOT SOLVED)

A new candidate source used the rational cyclic triple
x, -1/(x+1), -(x+1)/x. For omega^2+omega+1=0 its nonreal
resolvent is z(x)=a(x)+b(x)*omega, where

 a(x)=(x^2+x+1)/x,
 b(x)=(x^2+x+1)/(x*(x+1)).

The exact Sympy script `shanks_resolvent_metric_probe.py` factors
N(z(x)-z(y)) as (x-y)^2/[x^2*y^2*(x+1)^2*(y+1)^2] times an
irreducible residual of total degree eight, with multiplicity one. Thus this
is not an automatic rational-distance identity over the function field.
This is external algebra, not a new Lean theorem or a finite-size bound.

The rational secant of slope four through (x,R)=(1,3) on
R^2=3*(x^2+x+1) yields y=-2/13. At x=1 and y=-2/13 the two
threefold rotation orbits each have rational internal side lengths, but ALL
three cross-phase squared distances are nonsquares in Q:

 5809725/81796, 1269189/81796, 1026756/20449.

This is an exact failed metric control, not a random numerical search or a
rational-distance six/eight-point witness. Resultant and cyclic-root identities
do not supply the missing individual-distance squares. No size-growing rule
or unrestricted obstruction was obtained. Spec.lean remains unchanged with
its main sorry at line 187, and no new incomplete submission was made.

For a finite set S of positive rational parameters, partition it into
 t^4 < N, t^4 = N, and N < t^4.
The middle class has at most one element. If 2*n <= S.card, one of the
strict classes contains an n-element subset T. For ANY four parameters
from T, even allowing repetition, their product differs from N. The
product comparison is checked by taking fourth powers; no algebraic
fourth root or irrational parameter is required in the arithmetic proof.

For P(t)=(t,sqrt(N)/t), N>0, the earlier exact factor identities give
 rational distance(P(a),P(b)) iff (a*b)^2+N is a rational square,
 no collinear triple for distinct nonzero parameters,
 and no concyclic quadruple when a*b*c*d != N.
The new module supplies the actual Euclidean determinant bridges, rational
norm bridge, finite enumeration, and common-denominator scaling. Thus
`erdos213For_of_square_product_tuple` proves Erdos213For n from 2*n
positive rational parameters satisfying all OFF-DIAGONAL product squares.
No diagonal/antipodal square condition is needed.
